These methods trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and inference efficiency; recent work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, improved feature alignment, and tailoring teachers to be more 'student-friendly' to maximize transfer. Empirical results show that carefully designed KD procedures can retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and latency, enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across deep learning and NLP, KD comprises a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, online/teacher-free variants, and data-free synthesis—that trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while improving efficiency, but outcomes depend on matching objectives to student architecture, data availability, and task requirements. Practical success typically combines algorithmic choices with data strategies and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important as deep learning models grow larger and more computationally demanding, yet deployment requirements necessitate efficient, lightweight alternatives. Model compression through knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies across computer vision, NLP, and multimodal domains, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Bridging Performance and Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression in deep learning, enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones. This approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. The technique applies across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, demonstrating its versatility as a general-purpose compression method. By training smaller student models to mimic larger teacher models, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost without substantial accuracy degradation, making it essential for practical deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational structures, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while supporting constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques that transfer information from a larger, high-capacity teacher model to a smaller, efficient student model so that the student attains much of the teacher's performance while meeting resource or deployment constraints. KD includes matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or feature-based mimicry, multi-teacher and data-free strategies, and privacy-aware query/perturbation schemes. Empirical work shows KD is effective across computer vision and natural language tasks when teacher–student capacity, training data, and the distilled signals are chosen appropriately; theoretical and practical analyses identify limitations (capacity gaps, data regimes, imperfect teachers) and recommend combining KD with other compression methods and task-aware design choices to maximize real-world gains.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used training paradigm where a large, well-trained teacher model transfers its learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as a fundamental approach for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, making it a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practical Considerations, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of techniques—soft-target (logit) matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware strategies—enables deployment of compact models across NLP and vision while trading off capacity, robustness, and privacy. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, teacher and student design, data availability, and evaluation that probes rare or structural behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single recipe, knowledge distillation represents a flexible toolkit of complementary methods—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware strategies—that enable practitioners to deploy state-of-the-art models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of data availability and teacher-student design, knowledge distillation consistently achieves substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining much of the original teacher performance, making it indispensable for production deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. This approach involves training a lightweight student network to mimic a more powerful teacher network, enabling the creation of efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, addressing the challenge of maintaining high performance while significantly reducing computational requirements and model size.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention patterns, and operating in data-limited, privacy-sensitive, or federated scenarios. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful pre-training, KD enables production-ready trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and robustness to distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compression, Transfer, and Robustification in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique that not only enables compressing large models into efficient students but also serves as a mechanism for domain adaptation, multi-task transfer, self-supervised representation transfer, and improved generalization. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can reproduce state-of-the-art performance with far fewer resources in NLP and vision, but success depends on design choices such as which teacher signals to transfer (logits, intermediate representations, or adversarial/support samples), how to align teacher and student layers, whether to select or weight training samples, and how to handle heterogeneous data sources. KD can be extended via multi-teacher, teacher-free, black-box, and adversarial formulations, yet practical limits remain under data heterogeneity and some optimization/regulatization interactions. Thoughtful integration of KD with layer mapping, sample selection, data augmentation, and domain-aware trust metrics yields the greatest practical benefit.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in inference cost, memory requirements, and computational overhead across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational strategy for practical deep learning deployment, though its effectiveness depends on careful design choices, complementary compression techniques, and adaptation to specific task and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, demonstrating its versatility and essential role in practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and self-distillation, each adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints. While KD is widely applicable across vision, language, and multimodal domains, its effectiveness depends critically on careful alignment of teacher-student capacity, thoughtful selection of distilled signals, appropriate data handling strategies, and consideration of domain shift and fairness concerns. This position argues that KD, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression methods, represents a practical and versatile toolkit for enabling deployment of sophisticated models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though its success is neither automatic nor universal.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, with successful implementation requiring careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This approach enables the practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world challenges including computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, demonstrating its versatility and essential role in practical neural network deployment.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Default but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher-model performance when integrated into an engineering pipeline that attends to what is transferred, how data are selected or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on method choice, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, and it requires diagnostic evaluation for robustness, privacy, and domain-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across deep learning and NLP, KD comprises a family of techniques—logit/soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, online/teacher-free variants, and data-free synthesis—that trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while improving efficiency, but outcomes depend on matching objectives to student architecture, data availability, and task requirements. Practical success typically combines algorithmic choices with data strategies and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The toolkit includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate feature and layer mimicry, layer-wise or task-aware filtering, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data-free and synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical success depends on aligning what is distilled to student capacity and task needs, designing efficient training protocols, and mitigating limits such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization barriers, and degraded performance on low-frequency phenomena. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, empirical patterns, practical design choices, domain adaptations (including NLP and generative models), and open challenges for robust, deployment-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to mimic a larger teacher network, enabling efficient deployment of complex models in resource-constrained environments. This approach has become increasingly important for compressing large pre-trained language models and enabling real-time inference across various applications in deep learning and natural language processing. The technique addresses fundamental challenges in making state-of-the-art models practical for deployment while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Technique for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach is particularly valuable for enabling deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, whether applied to computer vision, reinforcement learning, or natural language processing tasks, represents an essential tool for bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student models through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. When applied with careful attention to task-specific design choices and combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for addressing critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Paradigm for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from complex teacher models to resource-constrained student networks, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in practical, real-world environments with limited computational resources. This technique has proven effective across diverse domains and application areas, making it essential for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Advances, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment and layer-wise mapping—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Recent algorithmic innovations address data scarcity, domain adaptation, and cross-modal transfer; complementary pipelines combine KD with pretraining, architecture design, and data augmentation to close the gap to teacher models. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and matching representational capacity between teachers and students; practical success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—including soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, online and teacher-free variants, multi-teacher schemes, and privacy- or communication-constrained protocols—enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. Successful distillation requires matching the distillation signals to student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with other compression mechanisms when needed. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common variants, representative applications, practical recommendations, and known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and self-distillation, each adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints. While KD is widely applicable across vision, language, and multimodal domains, its effectiveness depends critically on careful alignment of teacher-student capacity, thoughtful selection of distilled signals, appropriate data handling strategies, and consideration of domain shift and fairness concerns. This position argues that KD, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression methods, represents a practical and versatile toolkit for enabling deployment of sophisticated models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though its success is neither automatic nor universal.
