papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, enabling deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. The field encompasses multiple methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and feature-level imitation to multi-teacher pipelines and data-free approaches, addressing critical practical challenges in model deployment while presenting important limitations that require careful consideration.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses many concrete mechanisms (logit-level supervision, feature/attention transfer, layer mapping, synthetic-data distillation, multi-teacher schedules) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design to meet latency, memory, privacy, and interpretability constraints. When chosen and tuned for the deployment constraints and data regime at hand, KD routinely yields compact models that balance accuracy, robustness, and resource costs; however, careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data heterogeneity, fairness, and optimization dynamics is required to obtain reliable results.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a complementary technique but a central and versatile strategy that, when carefully designed with complementary compression methods, enables effective deployment across diverse domains in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique in deep learning that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach facilitates model compression without significant performance degradation, making it highly valuable for deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning, with various methodological innovations improving its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Superior Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Unlike traditional compression methods that simply reduce model parameters, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to transfer complex learned representations, enabling effective compression while maintaining or even improving model performance. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, making it essential for deploying high-performing models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted training paradigm that enables the compression of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a more efficient student model. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems. By leveraging teacher guidance during training, knowledge distillation achieves significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining or even improving student model performance, making it essential for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices and enabling practical real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile but Context-Sensitive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has demonstrated practical value across vision, language, and other domains by reducing inference cost, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and supporting distributed or privacy-sensitive workflows. However, its effectiveness depends strongly on data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and task specifics, and system constraints; thus KD should be applied as a composable element of a compression strategy rather than as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. This approach has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an indispensable method for modern machine learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, distillation reduces memory and compute requirements while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Techniques vary from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, and are combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision numerics, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, which data or augmentations to use, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to align teacher-student capacities. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical methods, domain-specific adaptations (including privacy- or data-limited scenarios), and recurring challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical element of model-compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, structured sparsity, architecture-aware design, and task-aware signal selection), KD yields deployable models that meet real-world constraints. At the same time, limitations remain: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher/student design require careful method selection and further research. I argue KD is indispensable but must be applied as a composable, task-aware strategy rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from one or more teacher models. KD has evolved into a flexible framework that includes soft-target matching, feature and layer imitation, multi-teacher strategies, data-free approaches, and integration with architecture search and other compression techniques. Across domains—especially natural language processing and computer vision—careful matching of distillation signals, data strategies, and student capacity yields practical, deployable models that approach teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and energy consumption. Remaining challenges include handling absent or private data, aligning inductive biases between teacher and student, preserving robustness and fairness, and automating task-aware compression decisions.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lower-capacity student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model deployment across computer vision and natural language processing while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be a core component of modern machine learning systems, supported by evidence demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse domains and methodologies.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of methods that compress large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across modalities and tasks, distillation operates as a flexible toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attentions, and adapting training data or objectives—to achieve favorable tradeoffs between model size, latency, and performance. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and task-aware design choices. While KD routinely yields strong size–performance gains, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled targets, data and augmentation strategies, and attention to distributional and low-frequency phenomena; these factors also expose open problems in representation alignment, robustness, and principled teacher design.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Composable, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students, enabling reduced latency, memory, and energy use while often preserving most task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data constraints and robustness concerns. KD should be treated as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Essential Techniques for Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful approach for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an indispensable technique for deploying large-scale pre-trained models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The method effectively addresses the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements without sacrificing accuracy, making it essential for real-world applications where inference speed and efficiency are paramount.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. The approach spans simple soft-target supervision to richer schemes that align intermediate features, layer mappings, and relational or ensemble signals. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and task-aware adaptations to meet constraints on latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Key open problems include principled selection of distilled signals, data- and privacy-aware workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automation of method selection for specific deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and essential technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to students through various mechanisms, addressing critical deployment constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and computational efficiency. Knowledge distillation has become a foundational methodology across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD encompasses multiple complementary strategies and demonstrates consistent empirical effectiveness, realizing optimal gains requires careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models at Scale
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of sophisticated deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods allow large, high-performing teacher models to transfer their learned knowledge to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the computational and memory limitations that prevent state-of-the-art systems from reaching practical applications. This survey examines the theoretical foundations, diverse applications, and ongoing innovations in these compression techniques across computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic and Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving competitive performance. Rather than a single recipe, knowledge distillation represents a flexible toolkit of complementary methods—including soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware strategies—that enable practitioners to deploy state-of-the-art models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When thoughtfully combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of data availability and teacher-student design, knowledge distillation consistently achieves substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while maintaining much of the original teacher performance, making it indispensable for production deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and representation-level imitation, relational or layer-wise transfers, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary methods (architecture design, quantization, data strategies), KD delivers strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, realizing these gains reliably requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. These approaches have demonstrated significant success across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, achieving substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy levels. This synthesis explores the diverse methodologies, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation and compression techniques in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with complementary methods—careful pretraining of compact architectures, feature-level and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free procedures—KD routinely yields deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD has important empirical and theoretical limits tied to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and optimization dynamics, so it should be embedded in a broader compression strategy rather than treated as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central strategy for compressing large neural models into compact students that retain much of the teachers' performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques—matching softened logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or synthesized data—that are applicable across modalities (vision, language, multimodal, graphs, and generative models). Practical KD workflows combine careful teacher selection, layer or token alignment, pre-training for the student, and complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning or structured sparsity). While KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs in production settings, its effectiveness depends on optimization choices, data availability, and mitigation of undesirable transferred behavior (bias, overconfidence, low-frequency errors). Current directions emphasize preserving internal representations, enabling data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and carrying forward robustness and interpretability from teachers to students.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity "teacher" networks to smaller, efficient "student" networks. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and reinforcement learning. The technique addresses critical challenges in practical deployment by reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring useful behavior from teacher models to students. Across vision, speech, and NLP, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. The technique encompasses multiple operational modalities — logits matching, feature mimicking, multi-teacher fusion, data-free synthesis, and distributed/federated protocols — and is best applied as an adaptable toolkit whose components are selected to match data availability, privacy constraints, robustness needs, and target hardware.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teachers to students. Over the past decade this family of methods has expanded from simple soft-label matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-free and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match capacities, and how to handle limited or sensitive data. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rare or structural behaviors, avoiding bias propagation, automating teacher–student design, and scaling distillation to ever-larger pretrained language models.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP systems, provided it is deployed as a principled, task-aware toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deployment in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks while preserving task performance. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining or improving performance. Across natural language processing and computer vision, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges by enabling trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, and accessibility for resource-constrained devices. Recent advances demonstrate that effective distillation requires careful attention to projector design, teacher quality, architectural choices, and task-specific formulations, making it essential for practical modern machine learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Advances, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment and layer-wise mapping—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Recent algorithmic innovations address data scarcity, domain adaptation, and cross-modal transfer; complementary pipelines combine KD with pretraining, architecture design, and data augmentation to close the gap to teacher models. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and matching representational capacity between teachers and students; practical success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression techniques enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. These approaches have demonstrated significant success across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, achieving substantial reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy levels. This synthesis explores the diverse methodologies, theoretical foundations, and practical applications of knowledge distillation and compression techniques in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments, particularly on edge devices and mobile platforms. By training student networks to mimic teacher outputs, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of maintaining competitive performance while significantly reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, information retrieval, visual recognition, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Promises and Practicalities of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. Empirical successes span vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, and variants include multi-teacher, self-distillation, feature-level and adversarial formulations. However, distillation is not a panacea: its benefits depend on how knowledge is represented (soft targets vs. internal features), on the student–teacher interaction mechanisms, and on data- and deployment-specific constraints (e.g., heterogeneous clients or low-frequency tokens). This article argues that KD is a powerful and flexible tool when combined with principled modifications — such as internal-representation distillation, projector ensembles, multi-teacher curricula, improved data augmentation, and task-aware distillation losses — but that practitioners must attend to these factors to realize reliable compression and generalization gains.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Path to Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes. The technique has demonstrated broad applicability across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, making it an essential tool for modern machine learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central tool for compressing large deep models into compact students suitable for deployment. KD encompasses multiple mechanisms (soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and data-aware variants) and has demonstrated effectiveness across domains including NLP, translation, computer vision, and medical imaging. At the same time, success depends on principled choices about what to distill, how teachers and students are matched, data availability, and task-specific adaptations; these considerations motivate a pragmatic, domain-aware KD practice that pairs distillation with complementary compression methods and targeted interventions to address known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and sometimes more robust models from larger teachers. Approaches span from soft-label and internal-representation transfer to data-free distillation, federated/distilled training for privacy and communication efficiency, and task-adaptive architecture search for large pretrained language models. Empirical work shows KD can improve inference efficiency with limited accuracy loss, transfer adversarial robustness, and enable effective low-precision and task-specific compressed models, while theoretical analyses and algorithmic variants clarify when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while transferring learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Practical Necessity with Context-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When carefully designed it enables substantial reductions in size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal cure: its success depends on what is transferred (logits, features, relations), teacher and student capacity and architecture, availability or synthesis of data, and task-specific phenomena (e.g., low-frequency words). Framing KD as a core, necessary element of compression pipelines — used alongside pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies, and evaluation focused on rare or safety-critical behavior — yields the most reliable tradeoffs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a range of objectives and design choices—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using ensembles or multi-teacher schedules, and combining with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—to balance efficiency and task performance. Practical success depends on matching teacher-student capacity, selecting what to transfer, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized data), and adapting distillation strategies to task-specific constraints. KD has been adapted across vision and language tasks and continues to evolve via techniques that improve transferability, training efficiency, fairness, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. The approach spans matching softened logits, mimicking intermediate features, adversarial and generative teacher-student games, and data- or architecture-aware pipelines. Empirical work shows distillation preserves much teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability, and the design of transfer signals. Ongoing directions include theory for when distillation improves generalization, task- and modality-specific objectives (including generation and multimodal transfer), and practical strategies for data-free or privacy-preserving compression.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of reducing model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining predictive performance. Across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, researchers have developed diverse approaches to transfer knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing quality.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile, broadly applicable strategy across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. The technique supports various compression objectives and has been extended to address privacy preservation, domain adaptation, and robust deployment in practical settings.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from cumbersome teacher models to lightweight student models through various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature imitation, and self-distillation. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as object detection and neural machine translation, making it an indispensable method for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches address critical challenges in inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in real-world environments with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

Knowledge distillation has evolved from simple output-level matching to diverse methodologies encompassing feature-level mimicking, attention transfer, layer alignment, and task-adaptive schemes, with broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and multimodal learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and sometimes more robust models from larger teachers. Approaches span from soft-label and internal-representation transfer to data-free distillation, federated/distilled training for privacy and communication efficiency, and task-adaptive architecture search for large pretrained language models. Empirical work shows KD can improve inference efficiency with limited accuracy loss, transfer adversarial robustness, and enable effective low-precision and task-specific compressed models, while theoretical analyses and algorithmic variants clarify when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students, enabling practical deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple strategies including soft-target matching, feature-level alignment, and intermediate representation mimicry, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and speech processing. Despite its widespread adoption and demonstrated effectiveness across diverse domains, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student capacity matching, and task-specific considerations.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.
