papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a technique for transferring knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This approach enables model compression while maintaining performance, making it valuable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and federated learning, addressing both computational efficiency and interpretability challenges in deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Driven Toolkit: Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core method for compressing large models into deployable students while preserving much of teacher capability. KD’s strengths arise from multiple mechanisms — soft-target regularization, intermediate representation transfer, and self-distillation — and its best outcomes come when distillation objectives are matched to the task, data regime, and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal fix: teacher errors, domain shifts, architectural mismatch, and data heterogeneity can limit or bias students, so practitioners must combine KD with complementary compression steps and rigorous evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical real-world constraints, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational and versatile strategy for model compression, though one that must be adapted thoughtfully to specific contexts rather than applied as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a niche compression trick into a broad set of methods that enable deploying high-performing but compact models across vision, language, and other domains. KD techniques operate at different levels (logits, feature maps, intermediate layers) and can be combined with pruning, quantization, or domain adaptation strategies to meet latency, memory, privacy, and cross-domain generalization constraints. When applied with task-aware design and attention to optimization and data constraints, KD yields substantial practical gains for real-world systems; however, mismatches between teacher and student capacities, data availability, and optimization dynamics require careful method selection and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex neural networks (teacher models) to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments, particularly on edge devices and mobile platforms. By training student networks to mimic teacher outputs, knowledge distillation addresses the fundamental challenge of maintaining competitive performance while significantly reducing model size, computational cost, and inference latency. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including machine translation, information retrieval, visual recognition, and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential but Context-Sensitive Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for producing compact, efficient models from larger teachers. It enables deployment of high-performing architectures under strict latency, memory, and energy budgets by transferring predictive behavior and representational structure into smaller students. KD encompasses a range of mechanisms—from softened logits to feature- and attention-level imitation—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. However, its benefits are context-sensitive: success depends on teacher–student alignment, the form of knowledge transferred, data availability and heterogeneity, and robustness goals. Practical adoption therefore requires method selection appropriate to task constraints (e.g., online vs. offline distillation, feature mimicry for representation transfer, or cross-distillation for few-shot regimes) and evaluation under distributional and deployment stresses.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while preserving task performance. A range of mechanisms — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, synthesizing surrogate data, and privacy-aware or multi-teacher schemes — enable practitioners to adapt distillation to domain- and task-specific constraints. Successful application depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, preserving rare or safety-critical behavior, data-free distillation, and robust cross-domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Through a blend of output-level supervision, representation matching, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical use combines distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and variants such as ensemble, federated, and data-free distillation to address heterogeneous deployment scenarios across natural language processing, vision, graph learning, and sequential decision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep neural models into smaller, deployable ones without substantial loss of performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory requirements, inference latency, and privacy concerns. KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, with continuous methodological innovations expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Comprehensive Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices and accelerates inference times for real-world applications. Through teacher-student learning frameworks, knowledge distillation transfers learned representations from complex models to compact ones, addressing the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across vision and language tasks.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical element of model-compression toolkits for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller students, enabling substantial reductions in model size, latency, and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, structured sparsity, architecture-aware design, and task-aware signal selection), KD yields deployable models that meet real-world constraints. At the same time, limitations remain: teacher–student capacity mismatch, data availability and heterogeneity, robustness transfer, and principled teacher/student design require careful method selection and further research. I argue KD is indispensable but must be applied as a composable, task-aware strategy rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables the practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. By transferring knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable versions without significant loss of task performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical neural network deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models. Across deep learning and NLP, KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse set of practices including intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher curricula, architecture-aware transformations, and data- or privacy-aware variants. These approaches enable deployment under latency, memory, and regulatory constraints while raising practical questions about teacher–student design, data availability, and robustness under distribution shift. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical strategies, empirical outcomes, and open challenges reported in the provided literature.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains. The approach encompasses multiple mechanisms and strategies, addressing critical real-world challenges including latency, memory constraints, privacy preservation, and computational efficiency. This synthesis examines the core methods, empirical applications, and practical considerations essential for effective knowledge distillation in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Techniques, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large neural models by training smaller students to capture teacher behavior, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Methods range from matching soft logits to imitating intermediate representations, self-distillation, multi-teacher schedules, and architecture-aware strategies. Distillation has been applied across modalities (vision, language, multimodal), tasks (classification, translation, question answering, detection, generative modeling), and distributed settings (federated and privacy-preserving learning). Empirical results show that carefully designed distillation pipelines can substantially reduce model size and inference cost while largely preserving accuracy, but challenges remain in data heterogeneity, robustness transfer, fairness, and principled teacher–student design.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. By employing multiple mechanisms such as soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and task-adaptive strategies, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements while enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining predictive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit encompassing multiple complementary techniques that can be combined to achieve substantial efficiency gains while retaining most of the teacher model's performance.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Critical Technology for Efficient Neural Network Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become an indispensable technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student models, distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression strategies, represents the most practical and versatile approach to achieving efficient neural networks across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student. A rich family of techniques—ranging from soft-label (logit) matching to layer- and feature-level imitation, attention-based alignment, adversarial transfer, teacher-free/self-distillation, and task-adaptive architecture search—has been developed to suit varied deployment constraints such as latency, memory, domain shift, and privacy. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance when distillation targets and alignment mechanisms are chosen to match student capacity and task structure; theoretical analyses and practical systems emphasize the role of soft targets as regularizers and the importance of representation-level transfer for challenging architectures like transformers and graph networks. Remaining challenges include principled teacher–student alignment, robustness under distribution shift, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical real-world constraints, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational and versatile strategy for model compression, though one that must be adapted thoughtfully to specific contexts rather than applied as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from complex teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation addresses critical deployment challenges including computational cost, latency, memory consumption, and device heterogeneity. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure from a teacher to a student. Recent work has expanded KD beyond matching output probabilities to include internal representation matching, flexible layer alignment, multi-teacher training, data-free approaches, and privacy-aware compression. These advances have been applied to NLP (notably BERT compression), vision, graphs, and other domains, while open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, layer alignment, and robust data-free training.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher-student recipe into a flexible family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing, resource-efficient models across domains including NLP, vision, and federated settings. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight architectures, transfer task-specific behavior, enable data-free or zero-shot transfers when original data are unavailable, and improve interpretability or domain generalization when adapted appropriately. However, distillation is not universally sufficient: optimization barriers, dataset artifacts, and bias transfer can limit gains unless addressed by careful method design. I argue that KD is a necessary part of any practical compression toolbox for modern deep learning, but must be combined with task-adaptive search, careful teacher selection, privacy-aware synthesis, and bias mitigation to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Default but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher-model performance when integrated into an engineering pipeline that attends to what is transferred, how data are selected or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on method choice, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, and it requires diagnostic evaluation for robustness, privacy, and domain-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi-Strategy Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. When treated as a multi-objective engineering pipeline—combining soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher fusion, and domain-aware adaptation—KD enables efficient models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across NLP and other modalities. Careful attention to teacher quality, representation alignment, and data selection is necessary to avoid degradation on low-frequency phenomena and domain-shifted tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, more efficient variants while preserving performance. Rather than a single canonical technique, knowledge distillation represents a flexible framework that can be adapted to specific deployment constraints, task requirements, and data availability scenarios. This article argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central technique for building compact, efficient, and practical models across vision, language, and multimodal domains when combined with complementary methods and task-specific design choices.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential for Practical Compression, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance through a variety of targets and training protocols. However, its effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signals, data availability, teacher–student design, and optimization; KD therefore works best as part of hybrid compression pipelines and with careful empirical diagnostics.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, computationally expensive deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to effectively transfer knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing fundamental challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This essay argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central and versatile tool in modern machine learning, particularly for practical deployment scenarios across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD enables deployment of strong models under latency, memory, and compute constraints across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. However, the empirical success of distillation depends on careful choices about what to transfer, the availability and nature of data, teacher-student capacity alignment, and task-specific constraints. When combined with complementary compression methods and appropriate training curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; conversely, poorly designed distillation can propagate teacher biases or fail to capture rare phenomena. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a core tool in model-compression toolboxes while emphasizing principled, task-aware design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and representation-level imitation, relational or layer-wise transfers, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary methods (architecture design, quantization, data strategies), KD delivers strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, realizing these gains reliably requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.
