papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary techniques—data augmentation, representation-level matching, online or collaborative training, and data-free strategies—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, achieving reliable gains requires task-aware choices about teacher signals, student capacity, and data availability; mismatches in inputs or internal structure and concerns about robustness and privacy remain important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational structures, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while supporting constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from an ad-hoc trick into a versatile, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models while preserving or transferring desirable behaviors. KD supports deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, and it adapts across modalities and tasks when paired with task-aware objectives and complementary compression techniques. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a foundational tool in model-compression toolkits and outlines practical emphases—preserving internal representations, using feature- and attention-level supervision where appropriate, supporting data- and communication-constrained settings, and designing teacher-student couplings matched to the target task.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP applications. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including NLP tasks, computer vision, federated learning, and various specialized applications, offering practical solutions for deploying complex models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across diverse applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining performance. This survey examines the fundamental principles, applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks. The techniques address critical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation while maintaining state-of-the-art performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Composable, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students, enabling reduced latency, memory, and energy use while often preserving most task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data constraints and robustness concerns. KD should be treated as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity "teacher" networks to smaller, efficient "student" networks. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and reinforcement learning. The technique addresses critical challenges in practical deployment by reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, computationally expensive deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to effectively transfer knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing fundamental challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This essay argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central and versatile tool in modern machine learning, particularly for practical deployment scenarios across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. The approach spans simple soft-target supervision to richer schemes that align intermediate features, layer mappings, and relational or ensemble signals. Practical deployments combine distillation with complementary compression methods (e.g., pruning, quantization) and task-aware adaptations to meet constraints on latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. Key open problems include principled selection of distilled signals, data- and privacy-aware workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automation of method selection for specific deployment targets.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This framework encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, feature alignment, and data-free approaches, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. Despite its widespread adoption and proven effectiveness, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student architecture alignment, and consideration of task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a versatile and practical family of techniques for compressing large deep neural models into smaller, deployable ones without substantial loss of performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, addressing critical deployment constraints including computational cost, memory requirements, inference latency, and privacy concerns. KD has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications, with continuous methodological innovations expanding its scope and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD comprises a family of methods (soft-target matching, intermediate-representation mimicry, attention- or module-level transfers, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data synthesis) and is most effective when matched to student capacity, available data, and task constraints. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss and, in some cases, improved generalization. Practical success requires careful design of objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free and self-supervised variants), and attention to fairness and robustness; these areas remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy). Progress spans soft-target matching, representation- and layer-wise transfer, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and integration with pruning and architecture search. Effective distillation balances what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and whether or how to use original, augmented, or synthesized data; when combined with careful pre-training and hardware-aware compression, distilled students can approach teacher performance while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Effectiveness, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for training efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models, with particular relevance to natural language processing and deep learning applications. This paper examines the evidence for the effectiveness of knowledge distillation approaches, explores various distillation methodologies including feature-based and adaptive approaches, and discusses practical applications in NLP tasks. While knowledge distillation consistently provides parameter reduction and computational efficiency, recent findings suggest the mechanism of improvement involves both direct knowledge transfer and regularization effects. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including machine translation, neural language models, and transformer compression, though careful consideration of teacher selection, optimization strategies, and hyperparameter tuning remains essential for achieving optimal results.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to resource-constrained student networks through various mechanisms including soft logits, intermediate representations, and feature-level alignment. Knowledge distillation has become essential for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational efficiency while enabling deployment on resource-limited devices without sacrificing accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Current State and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher models to simpler student models, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The method encompasses diverse strategies including soft-label transfer, feature-level matching, multi-teacher guidance, and data-free variants, with successful applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech processing. While knowledge distillation offers substantial benefits for model efficiency and deployment, its effectiveness depends on careful attention to design choices, teacher quality, data availability, and task-specific adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains. The approach encompasses multiple mechanisms and strategies, addressing critical real-world challenges including latency, memory constraints, privacy preservation, and computational efficiency. This synthesis examines the core methods, empirical applications, and practical considerations essential for effective knowledge distillation in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse mechanisms and has become indispensable across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and representation-level imitation, relational or layer-wise transfers, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary methods (architecture design, quantization, data strategies), KD delivers strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, realizing these gains reliably requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This framework encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, feature alignment, and data-free approaches, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. Despite its widespread adoption and proven effectiveness, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student architecture alignment, and consideration of task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that enables high-performing models to be deployed under resource constraints by transferring behavior, representations, or synthesized signals from larger teachers to smaller students. When treated as a composable, task-aware component of compression toolkits—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis—KD routinely yields practical size–performance tradeoffs. However, realizing reliable outcomes requires careful teacher selection, objective design, curriculum and data strategies, and explicit attention to failure modes such as optimization gaps, capacity mismatch, and the transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical yet Limited Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a widely adopted and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight students, knowledge distillation reduces computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. However, despite its substantial practical success, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and faces important theoretical and empirical limitations including optimization difficulties, teacher-student misalignment, data availability constraints, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and NLP. This approach involves training a lightweight student network to mimic a more powerful teacher network, enabling the creation of efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, addressing the challenge of maintaining high performance while significantly reducing computational requirements and model size.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Critical Strategy for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Methods include matching teacher output distributions, aligning internal representations, adversarial/generative teacher-student games, multi-teacher fusion, and data- or augmentation-driven pipelines. Distillation is widely used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on constrained hardware, and adapt models when training data is limited or sensitive. Practical deployments require careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare data and augmentations, and whether to combine distillation with complementary compression methods such as pruning and quantization. Open problems include data-free distillation, principled teacher design for student friendliness, robust multi-teacher aggregation, and aligning representations across heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in model size, latency, and computational costs while preserving competitive performance across diverse domains. The technique encompasses multiple operational strategies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis, offering flexible mechanisms to address latency, memory, and privacy constraints in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Practically Flexible Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large neural models into deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD techniques span matching teacher logits, aligning internal features, and using multi-teacher or teacher-free schedules; they enable large speedups and memory reductions, adapt to privacy- and data-limited settings, and have been successfully applied across retrieval, graph learning, generative models, and pretrained NLP transformers. The choice of what to transfer (outputs vs. intermediate representations), how to weight multiple sources, and whether to rely on original data fundamentally shapes outcomes. I argue that KD is indispensable for real-world deep learning deployment, but progress will require tighter practices for representation alignment, student-friendly teacher design, and handling heterogeneous or private data.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student models through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. When applied with careful attention to task-specific design choices and combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for addressing critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used framework for compressing large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and compute constraints. KD transmits predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher to student using diverse signals and objectives, enabling practical trade-offs between size and performance across modalities and tasks. The literature shows KD is effective when matched to task properties and deployment constraints, and that combining KD with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data and objective choices improves real-world outcomes. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, low-data or data-free settings, and principled selection of what and how to transfer.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation operates through multiple mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate representation alignment, and feature-level mimicry, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While knowledge distillation provides substantial practical benefits, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and integration with complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Task-Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. When applied thoughtfully—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and adapting procedures to task and data constraints—KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while dramatically reducing model size and inference cost. However, its effectiveness depends on design choices (targets, intermediate supervision, data selection) and on awareness of task-specific failure modes; KD is powerful but not universally automatic, and it should be integrated with complementary compression and adaptation techniques to achieve reliable, production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces the cost of large neural models by training smaller students to imitate higher-capacity teachers. The field has matured into a diverse toolkit that includes soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, data-free and federated variants, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, and task-aware architecture design. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can recover much of a teacher's performance across vision, language, speech, and graph tasks while enabling deployment under compute, privacy, and device constraints; remaining challenges center on data absence, inductive-bias mismatch, automated student design, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Across modalities and tasks, distillation reduces memory and compute requirements while often preserving most of the teacher’s performance. Techniques vary from matching output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, and are combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision numerics, architecture search) to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, which data or augmentations to use, how to select or adapt teachers, and how to align teacher-student capacities. This synthesis summarizes common mechanisms, practical methods, domain-specific adaptations (including privacy- or data-limited scenarios), and recurring challenges for applying distillation in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical real-world constraints, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational and versatile strategy for model compression, though one that must be adapted thoughtfully to specific contexts rather than applied as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. Across vision, language, graph, and generative settings, distillation methods range from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate features, using data-centric strategies (e.g., synthetic data or teacher-generated targets), selective sample weighting, and meta-learning of teacher behaviors. Distillation functions both as a compression tool and as a mechanism for regularization, domain adaptation, and privacy-aware transfer; however, practical success depends on teacher quality, data availability and complexity, optimization dynamics, and careful choice of distillation targets and sample selection. Domain-specific adaptations (e.g., for non-autoregressive translation, machine reading comprehension, and graph neural networks) show significant gains but highlight open problems in reliably preserving rare/low-frequency phenomena and in formalizing when distillation is most effective.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Strategies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that trains a smaller student network to transfer knowledge from a larger teacher model, enabling efficient deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices. This approach has become essential for making state-of-the-art models practical while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation addresses fundamental challenges in model efficiency by enabling reductions in size and latency without substantial loss in task performance.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling practical deployment while maintaining competitive performance. The techniques address critical challenges in modern deep learning, including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, and computational costs across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational and Practical Path to Efficient Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When combined with complementary methods—hardware-aware pruning, data augmentation, many-to-many layer alignment, and data-free distillation—KD enables practical deployment across modalities and devices. Responsible application requires attention to teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and bias transfer, and benefits from integrating KD into broader compression toolkits.
