papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Harrington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels and can operate at multiple levels (logits, intermediate features, or contrastive embeddings), enabling large reductions in inference cost and memory while often retaining most of a teacher’s performance. However, KD’s success depends on matching distillation targets, teacher-student capacity, data regimes, and deployment constraints; it is most effective when used as part of an integrated compression strategy rather than as a universal, plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or synthesized training signals. Across vision and language domains, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Empirical practice treats KD as a composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curricula, and data-synthesis strategies. Key practical considerations include choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), aligning teacher signals to student capacity, and handling limited or private data. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness transfer, principled target selection, and automating task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Strategic Approach to Bridging Model Performance and Computational Efficiency in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to lighter student networks, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from soft target matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated effectiveness across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications like graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Insights, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and natural language processing, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints through methods that include softened-target matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-augmentation and data-free approaches, and task-aware student design. Empirical results show KD can recover much of a teacher's performance when the distillation targets, data regime, and teacher–student pairing are chosen carefully. However, success depends on managing capacity gaps, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific objectives; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, or targeted data synthesis) yields the best practical trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning, enabling the training of smaller, more efficient student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has been extensively studied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, federated learning, and generative models, with various architectural innovations and theoretical frameworks developed to improve its effectiveness and applicability.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Strategic Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and self-distillation approaches. By addressing the critical challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on memory and latency-limited devices, knowledge distillation has become indispensable across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, providing solutions to critical challenges of inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Applications, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and resource use while preserving task performance. Distillation mechanisms include transferring softened output distributions, matching intermediate representations, ensembling or online teacher strategies, and data- or task-aware adaptations. KD has been applied across domains — from recommendation and ranking to object detection, non-autoregressive machine translation, and federated settings — and is often combined with complementary compression methods. Its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled targets, student capacity, and the match between training data and deployment conditions; these dependencies motivate pragmatic design choices and ongoing research into robust, data-efficient, and privacy-aware distillation pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Compression, Regularization and Privacy-Preserving Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for compressing high-capacity models into lightweight students while preserving or even improving generalization. Beyond simple teacher–student logits matching, KD can transfer architectural inductive biases, act as an effective regularizer, enable compression without access to original training data, and be adapted to low-data and multi-teacher settings. The choice of distillation objective, the availability of data, and the reliability of teacher signals determine success; consequently, a portfolio of techniques (data synthesis, augmentation, calibrated divergences, and confidence-aware aggregation) is needed to make KD robust and widely applicable in deep learning and NLP deployments.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile but Context-Sensitive Tool for Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD has demonstrated practical value across vision, language, and other domains by reducing inference cost, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices, and supporting distributed or privacy-sensitive workflows. However, its effectiveness depends strongly on data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, domain and task specifics, and system constraints; thus KD should be applied as a composable element of a compression strategy rather than as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile foundation for compressing large neural models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. As models grow in size and application contexts diversify, distillation provides a set of interoperable mechanisms — from soft-target transfer to intermediate feature matching, self-distillation, and teacher-ensemble consolidation — that can be combined with architecture search, quantization, and task-aware filtering to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, careful choices about what to transfer, which data to use, and how to adapt the student architecture are necessary to avoid failure modes such as degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena or overfitting teacher artifacts. A composable, task- and data-aware distillation strategy that integrates representation-level objectives, selective data curation, and architecture adaptation yields the best practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Framework for Deploying Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a single monolithic technique, knowledge distillation functions as a flexible, composable framework that can be adapted to specific task, data, and hardware constraints. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as the default strategy for model compression across deep learning and NLP applications, particularly when combined with complementary compression techniques and careful consideration of optimization and data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, sophisticated neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving significant reductions in model size and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an indispensable approach for practical deep learning and NLP deployment, supported by extensive empirical evidence across diverse domains and applications.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, addressing the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse mechanisms and has become indispensable across vision, language, multimodal, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Morrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Necessity That Is Context‑Dependent for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from teacher to student via softened outputs, intermediate representations, or task‑aware objectives, enabling reductions in size, latency, and resource use while often preserving much of the original performance. However, KD’s success depends on design choices—teacher quality and alignment, what form of knowledge is transferred, data availability (including data‑free settings), student capacity, and the task or deployment constraints—so it should be treated as an essential but not universally sufficient component of any compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains by transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student architectures. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, and data-free synthesis approaches. When strategically combined with complementary techniques and careful architectural design, knowledge distillation provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory constraints, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and natural language tasks. Over the past decade KD evolved from matching soft logits into a broad set of techniques—feature-level and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, curriculum and architecture-aware strategies—that collectively enable substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives, data regimes, and student architectures to deployment constraints; open issues include teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and adaptable approach to compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while retaining much of the original performance. When paired with complementary compression techniques and task-aware design choices, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, latency, and compute that make modern deep and language models usable in real-world, resource-constrained settings. Effective application requires matching the distillation signals to student capacity, careful selection of what teacher information to transfer, and awareness of data or distributional limits that can reduce or reverse gains.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Evidence and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible pathway to convert large teacher models into deployable student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting practical constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, complementary compression techniques, and task-aware data strategies. However, KD is not automatic: effectiveness depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. When used as the default compression tool, KD should be coupled with principled evaluation and complementary methods to produce reliable production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. A broad family of KD methods has been developed, ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and designing layer-wise or relational objectives. Practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthetic or unlabeled data) to produce deployable models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows KD improves generalization under limited-data regimes, recovers accuracy for low-precision networks, and can be adapted to heterogeneous or structured tasks such as graph link prediction. Key challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, dependence on data availability or privacy, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors; current directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, feature-level transfer, data augmentation, and task-aware objectives to mitigate these issues.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The field has matured from soft-target matching to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-representation matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, task-specific curricula, and data-augmentation or synthesis strategies. Empirical and emerging theoretical work show distillation can improve student generalization, robustness, and inference efficiency, but success depends on careful design of teacher signals, student capacity, optimization schedules, and data handling. Applications span computer vision, multimodal generation, ranking, and natural language tasks, and current trends emphasize making teacher knowledge easier for a constrained student to absorb while preserving fairness and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Integrated Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as an integrated engineering toolkit—combining logits-level transfer, intermediate-feature matching, architecture-aware layer mapping, and data strategies—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve most teacher performance. Real-world success requires matching distillation objectives to deployment constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness, and student capacity) and combining KD with complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be the central, configurable component of compression pipelines, used judiciously rather than as a single algorithmic recipe.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: A Multi-Strategy Prescription for Effective Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are most effective when treated as a multi-objective engineering problem rather than a single loss-matching task. Practical, robust compression for NLP and other deep models requires coordinated decisions about teacher construction, data and augmentation strategies, what to transfer (logits, features, or modules), and how to handle limited or absent training data. Combining dynamic multi-teacher selection, representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, and adversarial or meta-learned teacher paradigms yields students that retain more of the teacher's strengths while addressing common failure modes such as rare-token degradation and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, enabling deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. The field encompasses multiple methodologies ranging from soft-target matching and feature-level imitation to multi-teacher pipelines and data-free approaches, addressing critical practical challenges in model deployment while presenting important limitations that require careful consideration.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-label matching, feature-level mimicking, intermediate representation alignment, and data-free approaches. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized tasks, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational cost, memory consumption, latency, and enabling privacy-preserving deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications. While knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies and addresses critical real-world constraints, its effectiveness depends on careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific requirements. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be treated as a foundational and versatile strategy for model compression, though one that must be adapted thoughtfully to specific contexts rather than applied as a universal solution.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as crucial techniques for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. These methods address the fundamental challenge of reducing model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining predictive performance. Across various domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and machine translation, researchers have developed diverse approaches to transfer knowledge from large teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment without sacrificing quality.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Advances, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment and layer-wise mapping—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Recent algorithmic innovations address data scarcity, domain adaptation, and cross-modal transfer; complementary pipelines combine KD with pretraining, architecture design, and data augmentation to close the gap to teacher models. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and matching representational capacity between teachers and students; practical success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Indispensable Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference, reduces computational requirements, and supports deployment across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential, practically flexible tool for modern deep learning deployment, though its success requires careful consideration of what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from teacher models. This approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, providing solutions to critical challenges of inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Keystone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones without sacrificing much task performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, federated, and data-constrained settings, KD enables latency- and memory-efficient deployment, supports domain adaptation, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive and distributed workflows. Advances in KD emphasize not only learning from teacher logits but also mimicking intermediate features, designing student-friendly teacher objectives, and automating student architectures for specific tasks—yielding a spectrum of methods that together make model compression tractable in real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Multi-Strategy Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. When treated as a multi-objective engineering pipeline—combining soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, self-distillation, multi-teacher fusion, and domain-aware adaptation—KD enables efficient models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints across NLP and other modalities. Careful attention to teacher quality, representation alignment, and data selection is necessary to avoid degradation on low-frequency phenomena and domain-shifted tasks.

papers_seen.author: West
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving predictive performance. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student models. The method addresses critical challenges in practical machine learning deployment, including reducing computational costs, memory requirements, inference latency, and addressing privacy concerns. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized tasks, demonstrating its versatility and importance for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Effective yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. By enabling knowledge transfer through soft targets and intermediate representations, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. However, distillation is not universally applicable and requires careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints to realize optimal compression benefits.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.
