papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Practical yet Limited Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a widely adopted and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight students, knowledge distillation reduces computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. However, despite its substantial practical success, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and faces important theoretical and empirical limitations including optimization difficulties, teacher-student misalignment, data availability constraints, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-efficient student models through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. When applied with careful attention to task-specific design choices and combined with complementary compression techniques, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for addressing critical deployment challenges across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from Internal Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is typically conducted by training a small model (the student) to mimic a large and cumbersome model (the teacher). The idea is to compress the knowledge from the teacher by using its output probabilities as soft-labels to optimize the student. However, when the teacher is considerably large, there is no guarantee that the internal knowledge of the teacher will be transferred into the student; even if the student closely matches the soft-labels, its internal representations may be considerably different. This internal mismatch can undermine the generalization capabilities originally intended to be transferred from the teacher to the student. In this paper, we propose to distill the internal representations of a large model such as BERT into a simplified version of it. We formulate two ways to distill such representations and various algorithms to conduct the distillation. We experiment with datasets from the GLUE benchmark and consistently show that adding knowledge distillation from internal representations is a more powerful method than only using soft-label distillation.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. This approach involves training a smaller student network to mimic the output of a larger, more capable teacher network. The method addresses critical challenges in deploying neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining performance quality. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, machine translation, and information retrieval systems.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Effective Strategies for Deploying Deep Learning Models in Resource-Constrained Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices and edge computing systems. By leveraging various distillation methodologies—from soft target matching to feature-level alignment—this technique addresses fundamental challenges in deep learning deployment without sacrificing model capability. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph neural networks, making it a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning: Enabling Practical Deployment of Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a fundamentally important approach for reducing computational overhead and memory requirements of state-of-the-art neural models while maintaining competitive performance. Through systematic application in computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains, distillation has demonstrated remarkable effectiveness in creating compact student models that can operate within practical resource constraints. The technique's versatility, combined with its ability to achieve substantial efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss, establishes it as an indispensable tool for the practical deployment of neural networks in resource-limited environments.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to constrained student networks, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices across diverse domains. The approach encompasses multiple mechanisms and strategies, addressing critical real-world challenges including latency, memory constraints, privacy preservation, and computational efficiency. This synthesis examines the core methods, empirical applications, and practical considerations essential for effective knowledge distillation in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Sanders
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques form a practical, widely adopted toolkit for turning large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field has evolved beyond simple soft-label matching into a multifaceted set of methods that include intermediate representation alignment, progressive structural replacement, data- and privacy-aware procedures, and composition with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Across vision, language, speech, and generative tasks, careful choices about distillation targets, teacher selection, student capacity, and data strategies determine whether compressed models retain teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include principled transfer of rare or structural knowledge, robustness and safety under distribution shift, and automated, task-adaptive pipelines for heterogeneous hardware and privacy settings.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from cumbersome teacher models to lightweight student models through various mechanisms including soft target matching, feature imitation, and self-distillation. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as object detection and neural machine translation, making it an indispensable method for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Pragmatic, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large models into efficient students that can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When matched to task demands—through choices about targets (logits, features, or relations), data availability (real, synthetic, or none), and architectural strategies (progressive replacement, module design, or self-distillation)—KD reliably yields compact models suitable for real-world deployment. However, its effectiveness depends on careful teacher-student design, appropriate distillation objectives, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques range from classic soft-logit matching to feature- and layer-wise transfer, and they enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD's benefits requires task- and architecture-aware choices: what to distill (logits, features, internal layers), how to handle limited or private data, and how to align teacher-student capacities. When combined with principled practices, KD is indispensable for translating research-scale models into robust, efficient production systems.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained student models, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation represents a core strategy for addressing critical deployment constraints such as computational efficiency, memory requirements, latency, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized medical applications, demonstrating its versatility and practical importance for modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Promises and Practicalities of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. Empirical successes span vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, and variants include multi-teacher, self-distillation, feature-level and adversarial formulations. However, distillation is not a panacea: its benefits depend on how knowledge is represented (soft targets vs. internal features), on the student–teacher interaction mechanisms, and on data- and deployment-specific constraints (e.g., heterogeneous clients or low-frequency tokens). This article argues that KD is a powerful and flexible tool when combined with principled modifications — such as internal-representation distillation, projector ensembles, multi-teacher curricula, improved data augmentation, and task-aware distillation losses — but that practitioners must attend to these factors to realize reliable compression and generalization gains.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable, but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD provides a flexible toolkit—matching logits, aligning features or intermediate layers, ensembling teachers, and integrating with pruning/quantization—that often yields strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs for vision, NLP, and other domains. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on data availability, teacher-student capacity alignment, optimization dynamics, and the potential transfer of teacher biases; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful augmentation or data synthesis, and privacy-preserving or multi-teacher protocols when needed.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a mature, multifaceted framework with broad applicability across diverse domains, supported by both strong empirical results and emerging theoretical understanding of how and why these techniques enable effective knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, more efficient variants while preserving performance. Rather than a single canonical technique, knowledge distillation represents a flexible framework that can be adapted to specific deployment constraints, task requirements, and data availability scenarios. This article argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central technique for building compact, efficient, and practical models across vision, language, and multimodal domains when combined with complementary methods and task-specific design choices.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Strategy for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a powerful and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. While KD is not a universal solution and requires careful design choices, when combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, data-aware techniques, and task-specific optimization, it can preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference costs and memory requirements. This makes KD an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or synthesized training signals. Across vision and language domains, KD enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Empirical practice treats KD as a composable element combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, curricula, and data-synthesis strategies. Key practical considerations include choosing what to transfer (logits, intermediate features, attention), aligning teacher signals to student capacity, and handling limited or private data. Important open problems remain in robustness, fairness transfer, principled target selection, and automating task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Findings, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge from teacher networks. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and generative modeling, distillation methods have evolved from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations and adapting layer mappings for heterogeneous architectures. Practical results show large reductions in parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but challenges remain in robustness, student-friendly teacher design, and reliably transferring rarer or structural knowledge.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has matured from a single-purpose compression trick into a flexible framework that can compress models, transfer inductive biases, improve fairness and domain adaptability, and support continual learning across modalities. Its strengths come from multiple instantiations—logit matching, feature mimicking, contrastive representation alignment, module replacement, and automated search guided by distillation—which together make it broadly applicable for deploying high-performing models under resource constraints. At the same time, careful choice of distillation targets, mixture with hard labels, and awareness of teacher imperfections are key to realizing its benefits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Salazar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Default but Context‑Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers substantial reductions in size and latency while preserving much of teacher-model performance when integrated into an engineering pipeline that attends to what is transferred, how data are selected or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on method choice, data strategy, and complementary compression techniques, and it requires diagnostic evaluation for robustness, privacy, and domain-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single training recipe into a versatile set of techniques that enable deployment of large neural models under constraints of compute, latency, privacy, and heterogeneity. When combined with complementary strategies such as architecture search, progressive compression, and task-aware signal selection, distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance across modalities and tasks. Practical success depends on choosing distillation variants that match deployment needs and on designing teacher–student pairs and objectives that transfer the right internal and output signals.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques that enables high-performing models to be deployed under resource constraints by transferring behavior, representations, or synthesized signals from larger teachers to smaller students. When treated as a composable, task-aware component of compression toolkits—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis—KD routinely yields practical size–performance tradeoffs. However, realizing reliable outcomes requires careful teacher selection, objective design, curriculum and data strategies, and explicit attention to failure modes such as optimization gaps, capacity mismatch, and the transfer of undesirable behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Insights, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and natural language processing, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints through methods that include softened-target matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-augmentation and data-free approaches, and task-aware student design. Empirical results show KD can recover much of a teacher's performance when the distillation targets, data regime, and teacher–student pairing are chosen carefully. However, success depends on managing capacity gaps, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific objectives; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, or targeted data synthesis) yields the best practical trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Extensions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques enable transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, privacy). Progress spans soft-target matching, representation- and layer-wise transfer, data-free and privacy-preserving approaches, and integration with pruning and architecture search. Effective distillation balances what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and whether or how to use original, augmented, or synthesized data; when combined with careful pre-training and hardware-aware compression, distilled students can approach teacher performance while meeting practical constraints.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Design Caveats)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile framework for compressing large models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and representation-level imitation, relational or layer-wise transfers, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary methods (architecture design, quantization, data strategies), KD delivers strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, realizing these gains reliably requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: The Case for Responsible, Task-Adaptive Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an indispensable tool for compressing large neural models into compact, deployable students. When combined with representation transfer, architecture search, and data-aware synthesis, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, distillation must be applied carefully: mismatches between teacher and student internals, scarce or private training data, and distributional or low-frequency phenomena can limit gains or introduce undesirable artifacts. I argue that KD should be treated as a system-level design choice that pairs multi-objective distillation objectives with task-adaptive student architectures and privacy- or robustness-aware synthesis methods to realize reliable, production-ready compression.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models. When applied thoughtfully—combined with pre-training, representation alignment, sample selection, and complementary compression techniques—KD enables deployment of compact models that retain much of the performance of large models across modalities and tasks. However, KD is not a universal panacea: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and the choice of supervisory signal. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a primary engineering lever for compression and transfer but applied within a principled, task-aware pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD has matured into a flexible family of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention transfer, multi-teacher strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, but practical success depends on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and careful engineering of objectives and schedules.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. The approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, enabling efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across diverse domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a core practical strategy for model compression, supported by diverse methodologies, empirical validation across multiple applications, and a growing body of research addressing both effectiveness and limitations.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. This approach enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD encompasses multiple complementary techniques including soft-label matching, feature-level supervision, intermediate representation alignment, and data-centric strategies. The method addresses critical real-world challenges such as computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. Success depends on careful selection of transfer targets, appropriate teacher-student pairing, data availability, and matching distillation strategies to specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention patterns, and operating in data-limited, privacy-sensitive, or federated scenarios. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful pre-training, KD enables production-ready trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and robustness to distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for enabling the practical deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling significant reductions in model size and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Beyond simple parameter reduction, knowledge distillation encompasses diverse approaches including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, architecture search, and data augmentation strategies. The technique has proven invaluable across multiple domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech processing, addressing critical challenges in real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans practical recipes (logit matching, feature and layer-wise matching, projector modules), structural compression (architectural transforms, channel/filter reduction), and specialized strategies for NLP models (layer mapping for transformers and task-aware layer selection). Recent work also addresses learning dynamics and theory for wide networks, multi-teacher and meta-learned teaching, and scenarios with limited or no access to original training data. Empirical results show that careful choice of distillation targets, alignment mechanisms, and teacher-student curricula can yield compact models that retain strong performance on downstream tasks while enabling faster inference and smaller memory footprints. Open challenges include task-specific selection of distilled knowledge, robustness and generalization across distributions, and principled guidelines for architecture-aware distillation in transformers.
