papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from larger, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile, broadly applicable strategy across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. The technique supports various compression objectives and has been extended to address privacy preservation, domain adaptation, and robust deployment in practical settings.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable model-compression paradigm that transfers behavior from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce memory, latency, and compute while preserving task performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching soft-output logits to include intermediate-feature and layer-level matching, multi-teacher and many-to-many mappings, data-free and privacy-aware approaches, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical work shows distilled students can often approach teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and retrieval tasks, but practical success depends on choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are matched, and how limited or private data are handled. Key open problems include principled teacher selection, coping with data heterogeneity or absence, robustness to rare phenomena and bias transfer, and tighter theoretical understanding of when distillation improves generalization.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Effective yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. By enabling knowledge transfer through soft targets and intermediate representations, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. However, distillation is not universally applicable and requires careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints to realize optimal compression benefits.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students across computer vision, language, graph, and federated settings. When applied thoughtfully—combining representational distillation, pre-training of compact architectures, and task- or system-aware protocols—KD can retain much of the teacher's accuracy while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on what is distilled (outputs vs. internal representations), how teachers and students are prepared, and additional concerns such as adversarial robustness and bias that may be transferred unless specifically addressed.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become essential techniques for deploying large neural networks efficiently in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining predictive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world deployment constraints including latency, memory consumption, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit encompassing multiple complementary techniques that can be combined to achieve substantial efficiency gains while retaining most of the teacher model's performance.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a foundational, composable technique for compressing deep and NLP models: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and representations from high-capacity teachers into smaller students, and when combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis or adversarial training) it enables practical deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Realizing KD's benefits requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to handle data and teacher quality, and how to integrate KD into an end-to-end compression pipeline; when used with these considerations it yields compact, robust models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, size, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable, Central Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible, composable framework that transfers logits, intermediate representations, or synthesized signals from high-capacity teachers to compact students. In production settings KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when combined with complementary techniques (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture search, privacy-aware protocols) and when student objectives are adapted to capacity and deployment constraints. However, care is required to avoid transferring undesirable teacher behaviors (bias, overconfidence) and to address optimization gaps on low-frequency phenomena and under limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Technique for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Model Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach is particularly valuable for enabling deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation, whether applied to computer vision, reinforcement learning, or natural language processing tasks, represents an essential tool for bridging the gap between model performance and practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression: Strengths, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD methods—ranging from soft-target matching to representation-level imitation, self-distillation, and adversarial teacher–student games—enable substantial efficiency gains while often improving generalization. However, distillation's benefits depend on careful design choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers, and how to handle data or privacy constraints) and it is not a universal panacea: issues such as teacher–student mismatch, scarce or unavailable data, and task-specific optimization barriers require specialized strategies and evaluation. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible, composable framework that is essential for practical compression but must be applied with task-aware techniques and awareness of its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and allied model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more specialized models while retaining much of the original performance. The approaches span matching teacher soft outputs, imitating intermediate representations, many-to-many layer mapping, data augmentation during transfer, data-free distillation, and architecture-aware compression. Practical systems combine distillation with neural architecture search, federated or privacy-preserving protocols, and multimodal adaptation to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, heterogeneity of devices, and absence of original training data. This synthesis summarizes key methods, empirical insights, and deployment-oriented strategies developed to date.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model. The technique addresses critical challenges of inference latency, memory consumption, and computational efficiency across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, while supporting various practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. The technique encompasses diverse methodologies spanning logits-based distillation, feature and intermediate-layer matching, data-free approaches, multi-teacher strategies, and task-aware compression methods. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, making it an essential methodology for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, complex teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, graph neural networks, and recommendation systems, with variants adapted to different architectures and task-specific requirements. The technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural models in resource-constrained environments while managing computational efficiency, latency, and storage constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Synthesis of Recent Advances
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. These methods involve transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This synthesis examines the theoretical foundations, practical applications, and recent innovations in knowledge distillation across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains like object detection and graph neural networks. The review highlights mechanisms that enable successful knowledge transfer, strategies for handling heterogeneous model architectures, data-free distillation approaches, and applications to federated learning and multi-modal learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses multiple methodologies operating at different levels—from logits and feature maps to intermediate layer representations—and can be combined with complementary techniques such as quantization, pruning, and architecture search. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning, with successful implementation requiring careful consideration of teacher-student alignment, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific requirements.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are central for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring information from larger teacher models to smaller student models, practitioners reduce inference cost while preserving performance. A diverse set of techniques—soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate-feature and attention-based matching, layer-wise/task-aware alignment, data-free and generative replay strategies, multi-teacher or teacher-friendly training, and automated architecture search—has been developed and adapted to domains such as vision, generative modeling, 3D/novel-view synthesis, recommendation, graphs, and language. Practical success depends on matching teacher signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, handling limited or private data, and tailoring pipelines to task and architecture constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Applications, and Empirical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher network to a student network. This approach has become increasingly important for deploying deep learning models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. The field encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from feature-level distillation to cross-modal approaches, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning. Recent research has advanced both theoretical understanding and practical implementations of knowledge distillation, demonstrating significant improvements in model compression while maintaining predictive performance.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While the method transfers knowledge from a high-capacity teacher network to a smaller student network, recent research reveals significant complexities in how this transfer actually occurs and demonstrates diverse applications across computer vision and natural language processing domains. This paper synthesizes findings on knowledge distillation's effectiveness, identifies key optimization challenges, and explores innovative applications in healthcare, multimodal learning, and federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Comprehensive Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, making deployment in resource-constrained environments feasible without sacrificing accuracy. The method has proven successful across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains with minimal accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practitioners use a variety of objectives and architectures—logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, layer-wise supervision, and adversarial or ensemble-based transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Applications span vision, speech, recommender systems, machine translation, reading comprehension and multi-modal medical imaging. Key challenges include mismatches between teacher and student capacity, reliance on teacher training data, maintaining performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena, and the runtime cost of using large teachers during distillation. Recent work addresses these with task-aware layer selection, student-aware teacher training, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, and joint optimization of compression with distillation losses.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. By transferring soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational structures, knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while supporting constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The field has evolved from simple output-level matching to a comprehensive toolkit encompassing diverse methodologies and applications across deep learning and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Converging Strategies for Practical Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing classifiers into a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that enables deployment of large models in resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings. Advances span architectural strategies (progressive module replacement and feature mimicking), data-centric solutions (data-free and augmented distillation), teacher selection (ensembles and meta-learned teachers), and objectives that transfer robustness as well as accuracy. When combined thoughtfully — e.g., targeted feature-level objectives, careful data-generation or augmentation, and teacher optimization — KD enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. This article argues that best practice is not a single KD recipe but an integrated approach that matches the distillation technique to operational constraints (data availability, privacy, robustness requirements, and target hardware).

papers_seen.author: Zamora
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and efficient deployment of neural networks. This approach involves transferring knowledge from larger, more capable teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has been extensively applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in practical deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices across diverse applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains. The technique encompasses multiple concrete mechanisms including logit-level supervision, feature and layer-level matching, ensemble guidance, and data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression strategies and adapted to task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation routinely produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing computational requirements, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core but Contextual Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers. When combined with complementary methods—careful pretraining of compact architectures, feature-level and layer-aware objectives, multi-teacher or meta-learned teachers, and data-aware or data-free procedures—KD routinely yields deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. At the same time, KD has important empirical and theoretical limits tied to data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and optimization dynamics, so it should be embedded in a broader compression strategy rather than treated as a universal cure-all.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning and natural language processing. By training smaller student models to learn from larger teacher models, distillation enables the development of efficient yet accurate neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This synthesis examines the current landscape of knowledge distillation methods, their theoretical foundations, and diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. The field has matured from soft-target matching to a broad family of methods that include intermediate-representation matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, task-specific curricula, and data-augmentation or synthesis strategies. Empirical and emerging theoretical work show distillation can improve student generalization, robustness, and inference efficiency, but success depends on careful design of teacher signals, student capacity, optimization schedules, and data handling. Applications span computer vision, multimodal generation, ranking, and natural language tasks, and current trends emphasize making teacher knowledge easier for a constrained student to absorb while preserving fairness and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wang

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains by transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student architectures. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, and data-free synthesis approaches. When strategically combined with complementary techniques and careful architectural design, knowledge distillation provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory constraints, and privacy preservation.

KD techniques span soft-target matching, feature- and representation-level imitation, relational or layer-wise transfers, and data- or privacy-aware variants. When combined with complementary methods (architecture design, quantization, data strategies), KD delivers strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, speech, and federated settings. However, realizing these gains reliably requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or private data and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile approach for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms, enabling practical deployment across diverse domains. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in modern machine learning including reducing inference latency, memory requirements, computational costs, and enabling deployment on edge devices, while maintaining or approaching the performance of large teacher models across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying deep neural networks efficiently across diverse applications. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student networks while maintaining performance. This survey examines the fundamental principles, applications, and recent advances in knowledge distillation across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized tasks. The techniques address critical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and privacy preservation while maintaining state-of-the-art performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Merritt
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD methods span soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and correlation-based objectives, multi-teacher and online protocols, and teacher-free/self-distillation. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or teacher-generated examples), KD enables deployment of state-of-the-art models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints across vision, speech, and language tasks. Practical success depends on careful selection of distillation signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity and architectures, and handling data availability and domain shift; remaining challenges include principled signal selection, robustness and fairness transfer, data-free/privacy-preserving distillation, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performing deep models under computational, memory, privacy, and latency constraints. Work in this area spans traditional teacher→student soft-target distillation, distillation of internal representations, data-free or zero-shot approaches for when training data are unavailable, online and mutual distillation among peers, multi-teacher and ensemble-based strategies, and adaptations for domain shifts and task-specific requirements (e.g., non-autoregressive translation). Empirical findings emphasize that distillation often reduces training data complexity and transfers information most effectively when methods account for representation mismatch, data generation or augmentation, teacher–student capacity differences, and the distributional specifics of the task. Practical trends favor hybrid pipelines that combine soft-targets with representation matching, selective use of raw or synthesized data, and scalable online/ensemble procedures to support large datasets and heterogeneous deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP: Essential, Composable, but Not a Panacea
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students, enabling reduced latency, memory, and energy use while often preserving most task performance. Its effectiveness depends on choices about which teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data constraints and robustness concerns. KD should be treated as a configurable component of broader compression pipelines rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD includes techniques that use teacher output distributions, intermediate representations, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can improve student generalization, but success depends on optimization, data, augmentation, and how knowledge is represented and matched. Advances include representation-level contrastive distillation, data-mixing augmentations for more robust transfer, meta-learned teachers, and task-specific pipelines (e.g., NLP QA, graph learning) that adapt student architectures to preserve domain priors. Together, these results highlight practical best practices (careful choice of targets, augmentation, and teacher-student interaction) and point to open problems in aligning representations, handling distribution shifts, and designing teachers that teach effectively for resource-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Yet Nuanced, Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with architecture search, layer-mapping, or precision-aware techniques—enables compact models that maintain strong performance across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains requires attention to what signals are transferred, how layers are aligned, and how optimization and regularization interact; without careful design KD can fall short of teacher fidelity. I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational component of compression toolkits, paired with task-adaptive architectures and robustness-aware procedures to maximize practical impact.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a simple technique for matching teacher logits into a broad, practical framework for compressing large models and adapting them to deployment constraints. Contemporary KD encompasses soft-output matching, intermediate feature and layer imitation, online mutual distillation, data-free and zero-shot procedures, and combinations with pruning or low-precision quantization. Empirical evidence shows that when distillation choices (targets, data, teacher selection, and training curriculum) are matched to operational constraints, student models can retain much of teacher performance while achieving significant reductions in size, latency, and memory. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distilling robustness and rare phenomena, privacy-preserving distillation, and automating design choices across heterogeneous hardware and tasks. Practical success typically arises from integrated pipelines that combine multiple distillation signals with complementary compression techniques and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Strategic Approach to Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models while maintaining competitive performance across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech processing. By employing multiple mechanisms such as soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, and task-adaptive strategies, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements while enabling practical deployment of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Practical, but Context-Dependent
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, empirically effective route to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD encompasses a range of techniques (soft-label matching, representation mimicry, intermediate-layer alignment, multi-teacher/ensemble strategies, and data-free or online variants). While KD often yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on data characteristics, teacher–student capacity relationships, and deployment constraints. Best practice treats KD as a toolkit to be combined with targeted data strategies, representation-level objectives, and teacher selection or synthesis, rather than a single off-the-shelf solution.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in model size, latency, and computational costs while preserving competitive performance across diverse domains. The technique encompasses multiple operational strategies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis, offering flexible mechanisms to address latency, memory, and privacy constraints in practical deployments.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) consolidates a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger or differently-abled teacher models to smaller, faster, or capacity-constrained student models. Across logits, intermediate representations, layer mappings, and data-side strategies, KD enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models under constraints of latency, memory, or device heterogeneity. While KD is empirically powerful and widely applicable across vision, language, speech, and specialized tasks, its effectiveness depends on method selection, data regimes, and careful handling of teacher–student alignment and optimization dynamics.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling significant reductions in model size, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical practical challenges in modern deep learning deployment and has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central tool in modern machine learning, combining algorithmic innovations with thoughtful design choices to achieve reliable, production-ready compression results.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques enable deployment of large neural models in resource-constrained settings by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models. The field encompasses a range of mechanisms—logit/soft-target matching, feature and intermediate-layer imitation, layer-mapping strategies, and data-free or zero-shot approaches—and has been adapted to settings such as cross-modal transfer, graph-based tasks, fairness-aware learning, and generative model compression. Practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity and task constraints; remaining challenges include domain shift, privacy and data availability, representational alignment, and principled guarantees of robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Waller

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. Knowledge distillation encompasses a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches, ranging from simple logit matching to sophisticated intermediate representation alignment and task-aware compression strategies. The technique has been successfully applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and graph neural networks. By addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, computational cost, and privacy, knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.
