papers_seen.title: Layer-aware, Multi-source, and Data-efficient Knowledge Distillation for Compressing Pretrained NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large pre-trained language models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective compression requires going beyond matching final logits: it benefits from transferring intermediate representations, adapting to domain shifts, leveraging multiple reliable supervision sources, and handling cases where original training data cannot be shared. I argue that a practical, high-performing distillation pipeline for NLP should (1) align teacher and student internal representations with flexible many-to-many mappings, (2) weight and fuse signals from multiple teachers by confidence, (3) include domain-aware adaptation before distillation, and (4) incorporate data-free or privacy-preserving distillation options when necessary. Combining these elements yields compact models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, language, and specialized domains, researchers have developed variants that transfer prediction distributions, internal representations, or structural behaviors from teachers to students. This work summarizes practical motivations (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy), core technical variants (logit-based distillation, feature mimicking, self-distillation, ensemble and online distillation, and data-free approaches), empirical findings about when KD helps or harms (including effects on low-frequency lexical items and distilled-data complexity), and recent methodological extensions that relax dependence on strong teachers or original training data. The synthesis highlights open directions for large-scale, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive distillation strategies that are practical for production NLP and multimodal systems.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: An Essential Framework for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. This approach transfers knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. Across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, knowledge distillation encompasses multiple transfer mechanisms—from soft-target matching to intermediate-representation alignment—and integrates naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning and quantization. When carefully designed and applied with attention to teacher-student alignment, data strategies, and task-specific objectives, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning models into practical systems across industries.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The approach encompasses multiple methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level imitation, and attention-based transfers, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized domains. While KD delivers substantial practical gains in model size, latency, and memory requirements, its effectiveness depends critically on careful design choices regarding what knowledge is transferred, data availability, teacher-student alignment, and task-specific optimization strategies.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing inference latency, memory footprint, and computational overhead. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher strategies, and data-free approaches, with broad applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique addresses critical deployment challenges while maintaining competitive accuracy across various downstream tasks.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a versatile family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or synthesized data from a teacher to a student, KD reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s functionality. KD is most effective when treated as a composable core operation—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or task-specific alignment—and when its variants (data-free, online, teacher-free, or representation-based) are selected to match constraints such as data availability, privacy, or device heterogeneity. Despite strong empirical success, distillation has important failure modes arising from optimization difficulties and teacher–student misalignment; these warrant careful curriculum design, objective selection, and evaluation on task-specific failure cases. Overall, KD should be adopted as a foundational element of model-compression toolkits, used with explicit attention to its assumptions and limits.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in model size, latency, and computational costs while preserving competitive performance across diverse domains. The technique encompasses multiple operational strategies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, multi-teacher fusion, and data-free synthesis, offering flexible mechanisms to address latency, memory, and privacy constraints in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Comprehensive Overview
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, achieving substantial reductions in parameter count, memory consumption, and inference latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. The field encompasses diverse approaches including logit-level distillation, feature-based imitation, data-free methods, and multi-teacher frameworks, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and recommendation systems.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a core technique for producing compact, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher networks to smaller students. Across modalities and tasks, KD encompasses soft-target/logit matching, representation- and layer-level supervision, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-aware strategies. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial inference and memory savings, but success is task- and design-dependent: student capacity, pre-training, data accessibility, teacher–student alignment, and optimization choices strongly influence outcomes. Extensions of KD address domain-specific needs (e.g., graphs, federated settings) and emphasize composable, task-aware pipelines rather than one-size-fits-all recipes. Ongoing challenges include theoretical understanding of when and why KD improves generalization, mitigation of failure modes, and integration with privacy- and resource-constrained deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to making large deep models—especially pretrained language models—practical for resource-constrained deployment and domain-specific use. Work in this area spans teacher-student soft-label distillation, architectural compression and replacement, layer-mapping strategies, data-free and robustness-aware procedures, and combinations with low-precision arithmetic. Empirical results demonstrate substantial reductions in size and latency while often preserving most task performance, but practical challenges remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, access to original training data, adversarial robustness, and choosing task-specific compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are practical, broadly applicable strategies for deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Across tasks from retrieval and reading comprehension to multimodal generation and federated learning, distillation can preserve much of a teacher model's performance while cutting inference cost, enabling new real-time and on-device applications. Success depends less on a single canonical recipe and more on matching the distillation strategy to the deployment constraints and task: progressive structural compression, task-adaptive architecture search, layer- and feature-aware matching, careful treatment of soft targets and data, and privacy- or communication-aware protocols each address common real-world failure modes. Combining these complementary techniques yields compact students that are both efficient and robust for NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: An Integrated Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while transferring valuable learned knowledge. This approach enables practical deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications. By leveraging multiple mechanisms including soft output distributions, intermediate representation matching, and layer-level supervision, knowledge distillation addresses critical constraints of latency, memory efficiency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. A broad family of KD methods has been developed, ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and designing layer-wise or relational objectives. Practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthetic or unlabeled data) to produce deployable models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows KD improves generalization under limited-data regimes, recovers accuracy for low-precision networks, and can be adapted to heterogeneous or structured tasks such as graph link prediction. Key challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, dependence on data availability or privacy, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors; current directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, feature-level transfer, data augmentation, and task-aware objectives to mitigate these issues.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression transfer predictive behavior or internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the original performance. A spectrum of techniques—matching teacher output distributions, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or correlation-based feature imitation, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-side methods such as augmentation or synthetic example generation—have been developed and combined in practice. Success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to prepare or augment the data used for distillation; open problems include robust transfer under distribution shift, privacy-preserving and data-free distillation, and principled teacher design for specific student architectures and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Jefferson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical and Essential Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to student models, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This framework encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, feature alignment, and data-free approaches, with successful applications across computer vision, natural language processing, and other domains. Despite its widespread adoption and proven effectiveness, the success of knowledge distillation depends critically on careful design choices, teacher-student architecture alignment, and consideration of task-specific constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Foundational Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential and practical technique for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, this approach achieves significant reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies beyond simple logit matching, including feature-level alignment, attention transfer, and data-free approaches, enabling flexible adaptation to various deployment scenarios and constraints in domains spanning natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through multiple complementary mechanisms, knowledge distillation enables efficient inference and reduced computational requirements across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a necessary and central component of any practical model compression strategy, supported by diverse methodologies, extensive empirical validation, and addressing both the strengths and limitations of the approach.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. When combined with task-aware design choices—choice of distilled signals, teacher selection, data strategies, and architecture co-design—KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance while satisfying deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. To be reliable in production, KD must be applied as part of an integrated pipeline that addresses data availability, teacher–student capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-used technique for compressing neural networks and transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. This approach has been successfully applied across multiple domains including neural machine translation, language models, graph neural networks, and speech processing. The technique enables deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy through various knowledge transfer mechanisms and distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Unifying Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural models while preserving task performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables trade-offs among model size, latency, privacy, interpretability, and cross-device heterogeneity. Effective application requires choosing or designing KD variants that match the deployment constraint (e.g., layer matching for transformers, meta-learning teachers, data-free generation, or federated output sharing). When combined with complementary compression practices (progressive replacement, architectural search, or attention-based feature matching), KD routinely yields compact models suitable for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD comprises a family of methods (soft-target matching, intermediate-representation mimicry, attention- or module-level transfers, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data synthesis) and is most effective when matched to student capacity, available data, and task constraints. Empirical results across vision and language tasks show KD can substantially reduce model size and inference cost with modest performance loss and, in some cases, improved generalization. Practical success requires careful design of objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies (including data-free and self-supervised variants), and attention to fairness and robustness; these areas remain active research directions.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Practical Strengths and Limits of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible framework for compressing large models into efficient students suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When combined with complementary techniques—data augmentation, representation-level matching, online or collaborative training, and data-free strategies—KD yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance across vision and language tasks. However, achieving reliable gains requires task-aware choices about teacher signals, student capacity, and data availability; mismatches in inputs or internal structure and concerns about robustness and privacy remain important practical limitations.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Variants, and Domain Adaptations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable student networks by transferring information beyond hard labels. A family of techniques—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher curricula, task-adaptive compression, and domain-specific adaptations—enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, leveraging appropriate data or synthetic alternatives, and integrating KD with complementary compression methods and architecture search to meet deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Flexible Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones across modalities. When combined with complementary techniques—such as self-supervised teacher-to-student transfer, data-aware augmentation, progressive module replacement, architecture search, pruning, quantization, curriculum strategies, and teacher optimization—KD delivers strong accuracy/efficiency trade-offs while addressing constraints like privacy and data unavailability. This paper argues that KD should be treated not as a single recipe but as a composable framework that can be adapted to task, data, and hardware requirements to maximize utility in real-world NLP and deep-learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Vital Strategy for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for model compression and efficient deployment of deep neural networks. By transferring knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables significant reductions in computational requirements while maintaining or even improving performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is indispensable for modern machine learning applications, particularly in NLP and computer vision, where the trade-off between model complexity and efficiency remains critical for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) trains compact student models to mimic larger teacher models to reduce size, latency, and resource use while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD encompasses several transfer mechanisms (soft-target/logit transfer, intermediate feature and layer matching, attention-based mapping, and data- or model-aware curricula) and extensions (ensemble distillation, data-free or privacy-preserving workflows, and adversarial sample selection). Applied widely in NLP (including compressing large pretrained transformers), computer vision, and multimodal systems, KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—task-aware layer alignment, careful teacher selection or ensembling, and data strategies—to meet deployment constraints. Remaining open problems include principled choices of transfer targets, robustness under domain and data heterogeneity, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD encompasses multiple complementary mechanisms — soft-label supervision, feature- and attention-level imitation, layer-wise alignment, curriculum and meta-learning of teachers, and data-free or privacy-preserving variants — which together enable deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and data constraints. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling teacher–student architectural mismatches, and addressing robustness and data-availability challenges. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and practical considerations for KD in vision and NLP settings.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Practical and Principled Knowledge Distillation for Deep Models and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more interpretable models. When applied thoughtfully—matching architectures, choosing which teacher signals to transfer, and adapting to task- or data-specific properties—KD can preserve most of the teacher's performance while substantially reducing inference cost. However, indiscriminate application of distillation can harm performance (for example by overfitting to teacher errors or erasing useful data complexity); successful KD therefore combines algorithmic innovations (layer/feature matching, progressive replacement, adaptive search) with data-aware strategies (selective sample distillation, mixing raw and distilled data) and sometimes self-distillation to close remaining gaps.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central strategy for compressing large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a teacher to a student. Research over the past decade has produced a diverse set of distillation objectives (soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level imitation, contrastive and adversarial formulations), integration with complementary compression techniques (pruning, layer skipping, architecture search, quantization), and methods for operating under deployment constraints (domain adaptation, data-free distillation, ensemble teachers). Empirical studies across vision, language, multimodal, and industrial prediction tasks demonstrate that carefully chosen distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings yield substantial gains in efficiency with limited accuracy loss, while ongoing challenges remain in handling domain shift, teacher errors, and task-specific desiderata.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving much of the original performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, KD enables deployment on edge devices, addresses privacy and data-availability constraints, and facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures and modalities. This synthesis examines the core methods of knowledge distillation, key applications across domains, practical effectiveness, and important limitations and open challenges in the field.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, and task-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are fundamental techniques for enabling the deployment of large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, addressing the critical challenge of reducing model size while maintaining predictive performance. This review synthesizes recent advances in distillation techniques, compression methodologies, and their applications across various deep learning domains.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as an essential technique for deploying high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By enabling the transfer of knowledge from large, computationally expensive teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized medical applications, demonstrating its versatility and practical importance for modern machine learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical family of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student using a range of signals (soft logits, intermediate representations, layer-wise supervision, or synthesized data). Across vision and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, and it composes effectively with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Insights, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across deep learning and natural language processing, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints through methods that include softened-target matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-augmentation and data-free approaches, and task-aware student design. Empirical results show KD can recover much of a teacher's performance when the distillation targets, data regime, and teacher–student pairing are chosen carefully. However, success depends on managing capacity gaps, data availability, optimization dynamics, and task-specific objectives; combining KD with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, or targeted data synthesis) yields the best practical trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student networks, this approach enables practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse strategies spanning output-level supervision, intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher approaches, and task-aware adaptations, with successful applications across natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and specialized domains. The technique addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining model performance.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—commonly via softened outputs, intermediate feature targets, or structural behavior. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and recommendation systems, KD variants enable substantial reductions in parameters, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires tailoring what is transferred (logits, features, attention, or decisions), how teachers and students are aligned architecturally, and how data is used or synthesized; addressing teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and task-specific constraints is critical to robust, deployable compression pipelines. Recent work moves toward combined pipelines that jointly search or prune student structure while distilling appropriate signals, and toward adaptations for heterogeneous teachers, sequence tasks, and resource- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Effective Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compress large models into smaller, efficient students while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Empirical and methodological advances show KD succeeds when (1) the teacher signals are adapted to student capacity, (2) internal representations and attention patterns are aligned when architectures differ, and (3) distillation is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, low-precision, pretraining) and task-aware training regimes. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe: carefully chosen losses, multi-source reliability estimation, feature-level objectives, and integration with pretraining or hardware-aware compression yield the best trade-offs between model size, speed, and accuracy across vision, language, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible framework to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large, costly models (teachers) to smaller, faster models (students). Across modalities and tasks, KD can both preserve or even improve accuracy while enabling deployment constraints such as lower latency, reduced memory, quantized arithmetic, and multi-task or privacy-aware settings. Realizing these benefits requires matching the distillation strategy to task structure and student capacity: approaches that exploit multi-teacher signals, task-aware layer alignment, teacher adaptation, or self-distillation consistently produce better compressed models. I argue that distillation is not a single recipe but a family of practical, complementary techniques that — when chosen and combined thoughtfully — make state-of-the-art models usable in resource-constrained and application-specific scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Task‑Aware Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students while preserving predictive performance and enabling additional properties such as privacy, robustness, and fairness. When treated as a task-aware toolkit—combining soft-label matching, intermediate feature alignment, adversarial or generative data synthesis, and multi-teacher or curriculum strategies—KD can meet real-world deployment constraints (latency, memory, data access) across modalities. Practical success depends on explicit choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select distillation data, and how to align capacity and objectives between teacher and student; addressing these choices systematically enables KD to be both a compression engine and a mechanism for adapting models to constrained, private, or fairness-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a widely-adopted model compression technique that trains a smaller student model to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, with variants adapted to different architectures and specific tasks.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Multi-Objective View of Knowledge Distillation for Robust, Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical route to compress large neural models for deployment, but treating distillation as merely matching teacher output probabilities limits what can be transferred and how reliably the student will generalize. This paper argues that effective distillation should combine representation-level transfer, channel- and feature-aware objectives, confidence-weighted multi-teacher signals, domain adaptation, and training-time efficiency techniques, while explicitly attending to optimization gaps and fairness concerns. We synthesize evidence across methods and propose a prioritized, pragmatic pipeline for producing compact models that better retain teacher knowledge, scale in production, and reduce unintended harms.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models by transferring information from higher-capacity teacher models. Methods range from matching softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and extend to self-distillation, multi-teacher ensembles, data-free or few-shot workflows, and privacy-aware compression. Distillation is widely applied in vision, language, speech, and multimodal systems to reduce latency, memory, and energy use while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows distillation can improve inference efficiency, sometimes aid generalization, and enable robust or privacy-preserving deployment when combined with complementary compression techniques; however, challenges remain in teacher–student mismatch, sensitivity to data regimes, representation alignment, fairness and privacy guarantees, and principled theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the efficient deployment of large neural networks by training smaller student models to mimic the behavior of larger teacher models. This approach has become fundamental across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains, addressing the critical challenge of reducing computational overhead and memory requirements while maintaining competitive performance. The technique encompasses diverse strategies ranging from soft label guidance to intermediate layer alignment and operates through the transfer of learned knowledge from teacher to student networks.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods create smaller, faster models by transferring useful information from large teacher networks to compact student networks. In practice, KD reduces inference latency and memory use while preserving much of teacher performance; it is implemented through a spectrum of techniques (soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and data-side strategies) and is applied across domains from pretrained language models to domain adaptation and privacy-sensitive releases. Effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, data available for distillation, alignment between teacher and student architectures, and deployment constraints; open challenges include robustness under distribution shift, few-shot or data-free distillation, principled teacher design for constrained students, and privacy-aware protocols.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP (with Caveats and Design Guidelines)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically proven framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When combined with careful teacher–student alignment, multi-source supervision, privacy-preserving mechanisms, and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable size–performance tradeoffs across vision, language, generative, and recommendation tasks. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. KD should therefore be the default tool for model compression in production, used alongside complementary techniques and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.
