papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Superior Approach to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile technique for compressing deep neural networks and transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models. Unlike traditional compression methods that simply reduce model parameters, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to transfer complex learned representations, enabling effective compression while maintaining or even improving model performance. This approach has been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, making it essential for deploying high-performing models on resource-constrained devices.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core and Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has evolved from a single-purpose compression technique into a comprehensive and adaptable framework for deploying efficient deep neural networks across diverse applications. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student models, knowledge distillation enables significant reductions in computational requirements and model size while maintaining or even improving predictive performance. This approach addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices, making it essential for real-world applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output logits to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate representation alignment, layer- and attention-wise mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data synthesis or augmentation strategies. In practice KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-specific design. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rarer or structural knowledge, operating without original training data, and automating task-aware compression decisions.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD has matured into a flexible family of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention transfer, multi-teacher strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, but practical success depends on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and careful engineering of objectives and schedules.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of theoretical and practical approaches for producing smaller, faster, or more specialized models from larger ones. Work in this area ranges from formal analyses of when and why distillation helps, to engineering advances that reduce runtime cost, enable training without original data, transfer across modalities, improve robustness and privacy, and tailor distilled models for downstream tasks or heterogeneous deployment environments. Practical methods include mimicking logits, matching intermediate representations or attention, progressively replacing modules, using student-focused filtering of teacher signals, and leveraging data augmentation or online collaboration between models. Emerging directions emphasize theoretical understanding, task-aware selection of distilled information, privacy-preserving or data-free pipelines, and retaining adversarial robustness while reducing model size.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Advancing Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Systems
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach involves transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a compact student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices without sacrificing accuracy. While the foundational concept has been widely applied across computer vision, recommender systems, and natural language processing, recent advances have introduced sophisticated variations and domain-specific adaptations. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of knowledge distillation methodologies, including selective distillation approaches, cross-modal knowledge transfer, adversarial learning frameworks, and specialized applications to transformer-based architectures and sequential tasks.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. Rather than a monolithic approach, knowledge distillation represents a flexible family of methods that transfer various forms of knowledge—from output distributions to intermediate representations—from teacher to student models. This technique enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and addresses critical challenges in reducing computational costs, latency, and memory requirements without significant accuracy loss. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and federated learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective framework for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses a range of objectives and design choices—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using ensembles or multi-teacher schedules, and combining with architecture search, pruning, or quantization—to balance efficiency and task performance. Practical success depends on matching teacher-student capacity, selecting what to transfer, handling data availability (including data-free or synthesized data), and adapting distillation strategies to task-specific constraints. KD has been adapted across vision and language tasks and continues to evolve via techniques that improve transferability, training efficiency, fairness, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, latency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices and recognition of important limitations that require pragmatic, task-adaptive application strategies.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Effective yet Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. By enabling knowledge transfer through soft targets and intermediate representations, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. However, distillation is not universally applicable and requires careful design choices regarding teacher-student alignment, data availability, and task-specific constraints to realize optimal compression benefits.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring task-relevant information. Across deep learning and NLP, KD encompasses output-level soft-label matching, feature- and layer-level supervision, architecture-aware procedures, and data-centric strategies (including pretraining and synthetic data). These techniques enable deployment in resource-constrained settings, often preserving much of a teacher’s performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy use. Practical success depends on choices about what teacher signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student components, whether to pretrain students, and how to handle limited or private data. Current advances broaden KD’s role beyond compression to include regularization, robustness, fairness-aware transfer, and privacy-preserving forms of model adaptation, while open challenges remain in principled selection of transfer targets, handling distribution shift, and automating task-adaptive compression.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transform large, expensive models into smaller, faster, or otherwise more deployable models by transferring knowledge from one model (teacher) to another (student). Research over the past decade has produced a spectrum of methods: representation- and layer-matching, soft-target regularization and teacher-free variants, data-free and adversarial sample synthesis, many-to-many layer alignment for transformer compression, and task-adaptive architecture search with distillation objectives. These approaches address practical constraints—limited compute, privacy of training data, heterogeneous devices, and task-specific requirements—while revealing theoretical connections between KD and regularization. Empirical work shows KD is effective across vision and language tasks, can enable competitive small models for NLP, and remains central to specialized pipelines such as non-autoregressive translation and transformer pruning. Open directions include better matching of inductive biases between teacher and student, principled handling of data absence or privacy, and automated, task-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Espinoza
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical but Context-Dependent Approach for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central and widely-adopted technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables high-performing deep learning systems to operate in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. This approach encompasses multiple methodologies spanning logit matching, feature alignment, and representation-level transfer, with proven empirical success in reducing model size, latency, and memory consumption. However, knowledge distillation is not a universal solution and requires careful design choices, thoughtful data strategies, and integration with complementary compression techniques to effectively balance accuracy, efficiency, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Multipurpose Tool for Model Compression and Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a principled, adaptable framework that can both reduce model size and provide transfer, robustness, and deployment advantages when combined with complementary techniques. A practical KD-centered strategy emphasizes transferring intermediate representations in addition to logits, leveraging multiple and domain-aware teachers, accommodating imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and adapting to constraints such as privacy or federated settings. When KD is used alongside pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design, it enables compact models that approach the performance of much larger teachers while meeting latency, memory, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from teacher models. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes representation- and layer-level transfer, architecture-aware transformations, data- and teacher-selection strategies, and domain-adaptive procedures. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can yield large efficiency gains while retaining most teacher performance, but practical success depends on careful choices about what is distilled, how teachers and students are prepared, and how data or synthetic examples are used.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling efficient knowledge transfer from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, this approach directly addresses critical real-world deployment challenges including computational cost, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy concerns. The technique has proven essential across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, making it indispensable for modern machine learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models into smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from a teacher to a student. Across vision, language, graph, generative, and neural-architecture-search settings, methods vary from matching soft labels to aligning intermediate features, using attention-based layer projection, contrastive alignment, and optimization-aware divergences. Practical adaptations address data availability, privacy, and efficiency constraints, while empirical and theoretical analyses reveal optimization limits, dataset and heterogeneity sensitivities, and opportunities from meta-learning teachers and task-specific design. Despite broad success, key open problems remain in reliably preserving teacher knowledge, designing data- and privacy-aware protocols, and tailoring distillation to domain-specific structures.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large deep neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models while preserving predictive performance. Applications span computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and other domains, with diverse approaches adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression have become indispensable techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these methods enable significant reductions in computational requirements, memory usage, and latency while maintaining competitive accuracy. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile and practical family of complementary techniques that, when thoughtfully combined, make sophisticated models deployable across diverse domains including NLP, computer vision, and specialized applications, while addressing critical real-world constraints such as privacy, data heterogeneity, and hardware limitations.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Methods, Adaptations, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become standard tools to transfer knowledge from large, high-capacity models to smaller, efficient models suitable for deployment. Research across modalities and tasks has developed variants that go beyond matching output logits, including feature mimicking, attention- and channel-wise transfers, layer alignment strategies, and task-adaptive or domain-aware schemes. These approaches aim to preserve predictive accuracy and representational structure while reducing storage, computation, and latency. Practical advances demonstrate that carefully designed distillation objectives and mapping strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance on classification, ranking, language, speech, graph, and generative tasks, and that adapting distillation to task or domain specifics improves real-world applicability.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential, Yet Nuanced, Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile strategy for compressing large neural networks into smaller models suitable for resource-constrained deployment. KD can transfer predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or task-specific structure from teacher to student, and—when combined with architecture search, layer-mapping, or precision-aware techniques—enables compact models that maintain strong performance across vision and language tasks. However, realizing those gains requires attention to what signals are transferred, how layers are aligned, and how optimization and regularization interact; without careful design KD can fall short of teacher fidelity. I argue that KD should be treated as a foundational component of compression toolkits, paired with task-adaptive architectures and robustness-aware procedures to maximize practical impact.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened output logits to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate representation alignment, layer- and attention-wise mapping, multi-teacher schedules, and data synthesis or augmentation strategies. In practice KD enables substantial reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability, teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-specific design. Remaining challenges include robustly transferring rarer or structural knowledge, operating without original training data, and automating task-aware compression decisions.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models. Through a blend of output-level supervision, representation matching, and task- or architecture-aware adaptations, distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical use combines distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and variants such as ensemble, federated, and data-free distillation to address heterogeneous deployment scenarios across natural language processing, vision, graph learning, and sequential decision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely adopted family of techniques for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models that meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. KD methods include matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention, adversarial and online schemes, and data-free or zero-shot approaches; they are often combined with architecture search, pruning, and quantization to reach target resource budgets. Across vision, language, generative models, and federated settings, practical success hinges on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data availability and domain shift, and mitigating the transfer of teacher errors or undesirable behavior. While KD routinely produces favorable efficiency–accuracy tradeoffs, remaining challenges include principled teacher–student design, robustness under distribution shift, and reliable transfer of structural or low-frequency knowledge.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, and multimodal settings. KD encompasses matching teacher soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention patterns, and operating in data-limited, privacy-sensitive, or federated scenarios. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture search, and careful pre-training, KD enables production-ready trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, practical deployment requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability, and robustness to distribution shift and low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, powerful models into smaller, faster models by transferring information beyond hard labels. In NLP and broader deep learning, KD has been applied to pre-trained transformers, sequence models, ensembles, and cross-modal architectures using techniques that include soft-label matching, intermediate feature supervision, progressive module replacement, architecture search, data augmentation, and adversarial sample selection. These methods trade off fidelity to the teacher, student capacity, and inference efficiency; recent work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, improved feature alignment, and tailoring teachers to be more 'student-friendly' to maximize transfer. Empirical results show that carefully designed KD procedures can retain much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and latency, enabling deployment in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster, or more resource-efficient models for deployment. Work in this area spans methods that transfer teacher output distributions, match intermediate representations, perform layer- or module-level supervision, and combine compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) with distillation objectives. Recent advances emphasize task-aware selection of teacher signals, data-free or privacy-preserving distillation, the role of data augmentation and training heuristics, and hardware-aware pruning strategies. Empirical results show that careful distillation pipelines can retain most teacher performance while substantially reducing size and latency, but open challenges remain in handling mismatched teacher–student capacity, limited or absent training data, robustness on rare phenomena, and joint optimization for heterogeneous hardware.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of methods that compress large, high-performing neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across modalities and tasks, distillation operates as a flexible toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attentions, and adapting training data or objectives—to achieve favorable tradeoffs between model size, latency, and performance. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture changes) and task-aware design choices. While KD routinely yields strong size–performance gains, its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, the choice of distilled targets, data and augmentation strategies, and attention to distributional and low-frequency phenomena; these factors also expose open problems in representation alignment, robustness, and principled teacher design.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

This approach enables substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference latency while maintaining competitive predictive performance. While knowledge distillation is not a universal solution, when carefully combined with complementary strategies such as representation-level transfer, task-specific optimization, and data-aware techniques, it becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models into practical systems across diverse domains.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble models into smaller, faster students by transferring information beyond hard labels. KD includes techniques that use teacher output distributions, intermediate representations, contrastive objectives, data augmentation, and multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can improve student generalization, but success depends on optimization, data, augmentation, and how knowledge is represented and matched. Advances include representation-level contrastive distillation, data-mixing augmentations for more robust transfer, meta-learned teachers, and task-specific pipelines (e.g., NLP QA, graph learning) that adapt student architectures to preserve domain priors. Together, these results highlight practical best practices (careful choice of targets, augmentation, and teacher-student interaction) and point to open problems in aligning representations, handling distribution shifts, and designing teachers that teach effectively for resource-constrained deployments.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Dependent Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated framework for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. KD spans a range of mechanisms—from softened-output matching to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While KD often enables deployable students that approach teacher performance, success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle data availability or privacy constraints, and how to pair distillation with complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential and Practical Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practically indispensable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should serve as the default strategy for model compression in modern deep learning and NLP systems, provided it is deployed as a principled, task-aware toolkit rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Applications, and Practical Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks while maintaining competitive performance. The technique has demonstrated broad applicability across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and specialized applications, addressing critical challenges in model deployment such as computational cost, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Strategic Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and self-distillation approaches. By addressing the critical challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on memory and latency-limited devices, knowledge distillation has become indispensable across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from large, complex teacher models to compact student models while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying deep learning systems across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, machine translation, and speech recognition, providing a practical pathway for creating efficient models without substantial accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Practical Paths and Limits for Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) remains a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving performance. KD has evolved from simple logit matching to diverse strategies that address data availability, task specificity, representation-level transfer, and architectural mismatches. However, fundamental limits—especially under heterogeneous data or federated settings—and practical challenges such as selecting useful teacher signal and coping with student capacity remain. A pragmatic approach combines data-aware or data-free sample generation, representation- and layer-level objectives, and task-aware filtering to maximize transfer while respecting privacy, compute, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models. This approach has become essential for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methods ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment and task-aware compression strategies, and has been successfully applied across multiple domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and specialized applications. By addressing critical deployment constraints such as latency, memory, computational cost, and privacy, knowledge distillation has emerged as a foundational technique in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach enables the transfer of knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models through various mechanisms, addressing the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech processing, and medical imaging, making it an essential paradigm for practical deep learning deployment.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical and Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a practical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments. The technique encompasses multiple methodologies—including soft-target matching, feature mimicking, layer-wise alignment, and data-free synthesis—and has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and reinforcement learning. Recent research demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression heuristic but a flexible toolkit that, when carefully designed and integrated with complementary techniques, can achieve student models that approach teacher performance while meeting practical deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive and representational knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models so compact systems can run under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The literature shows a wide family of methods — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational and task-specific mappings, self- and multi-teacher schemes, and data-side strategies such as augmentation, synthetic data, or pre-training compact architectures — that together enable strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. Empirical successes span vision, speech, recommendation, and natural language tasks, but open issues remain, including teacher–student mismatch, robustness under distribution shift, limited or absent training data, and principled design of what to transfer for particular student capacities. Practical deployments benefit from combining complementary techniques (representation-level objectives, augmentation-aware distillation, pre-training of small models, and continual or task-adaptive strategies) and from careful tuning of teacher construction, data, and transfer objectives.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient models by transferring predictive behavior and intermediate representations from teacher to student. Across computer vision, NLP, and generative modeling, distillation methods include softened-output matching, intermediate feature or attention transfer, layer-wise alignment, and online or adaptive teacher-student schemes. Practical pipelines often combine distillation with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and emphasize task-aware choices of distillation targets, data strategies, and teacher design to maximize student performance under resource constraints. Important open challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, reducing reliance on teacher data, and ensuring robustness and fidelity on low-frequency or safety-critical phenomena.
