papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as fundamental techniques for deploying large neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches address critical challenges in inference speed, memory consumption, and computational resource requirements. The techniques have been successfully applied across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and specialized applications, enabling practical deployment of sophisticated deep learning systems in real-world environments with limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression represent a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, more complex neural networks to smaller, more efficient models. These approaches enable deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation has evolved from a heuristic compression technique to a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, privacy preservation, and task-specific performance optimization.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—commonly via softened outputs, intermediate feature targets, or structural behavior. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and recommendation systems, KD variants enable substantial reductions in parameters, memory, and latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical application requires tailoring what is transferred (logits, features, attention, or decisions), how teachers and students are aligned architecturally, and how data is used or synthesized; addressing teacher–student mismatch, limited or private data, and task-specific constraints is critical to robust, deployable compression pipelines. Recent work moves toward combined pipelines that jointly search or prune student structure while distilling appropriate signals, and toward adaptations for heterogeneous teachers, sequence tasks, and resource- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Bridging the Gap Between Performance and Efficiency in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing, enabling the transfer of knowledge from larger, well-trained teacher networks to smaller, more efficient student networks. This technique addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated neural networks on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive performance. Through various methodological innovations ranging from attention-based mechanisms to adversarial approaches, knowledge distillation has demonstrated its effectiveness across multiple domains including computer vision, machine translation, and NLP tasks. The field continues to evolve with advances in online distillation, multi-modal approaches, and task-aware compression strategies that optimize the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD uses a range of transfer targets and training schemes to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size, and it is routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints. While KD consistently enables substantial efficiency gains across vision, language, and graph domains, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and how to handle limited or sensitive data.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Keystone for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential family of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones without sacrificing much task performance. Across supervised, self-supervised, federated, and data-constrained settings, KD enables latency- and memory-efficient deployment, supports domain adaptation, and can be adapted to privacy-sensitive and distributed workflows. Advances in KD emphasize not only learning from teacher logits but also mimicking intermediate features, designing student-friendly teacher objectives, and automating student architectures for specific tasks—yielding a spectrum of methods that together make model compression tractable in real-world NLP and vision systems.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Essential Framework for Model Compression and Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers learned representations from complex teacher networks to simpler student networks, enabling efficient deployment across resource-constrained environments in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. The method addresses critical practical challenges in model deployment including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency reduction without sacrificing accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation facilitates knowledge transfer across architectures, improves model robustness, and supports learning from ensembles, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Fundamental Approach to Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a transformative technique for compressing neural networks while maintaining predictive performance. By enabling knowledge transfer from large teacher models to compact student networks, distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying sophisticated deep learning systems on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential methodology for practical machine learning deployment, offering significant advantages in model size reduction, computational efficiency, and accessibility across diverse application domains from natural language processing to computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity "teacher" networks to smaller, efficient "student" networks. This approach enables the deployment of deep learning models in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized applications such as recommendation systems and reinforcement learning. The technique addresses critical challenges in practical deployment by reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of methods for producing smaller, faster, and sometimes more robust models from larger teachers. Approaches span from soft-label and internal-representation transfer to data-free distillation, federated/distilled training for privacy and communication efficiency, and task-adaptive architecture search for large pretrained language models. Empirical work shows KD can improve inference efficiency with limited accuracy loss, transfer adversarial robustness, and enable effective low-precision and task-specific compressed models, while theoretical analyses and algorithmic variants clarify when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Practice, and Open Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster models by transferring information from a teacher to a student. KD techniques operate at multiple levels — soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relations, or via self- and online-distillation — and are widely used to enable deployment in resource- and latency-constrained settings across NLP, speech, vision, and multimodal tasks. Empirical work shows that carefully designed distillation pipelines can preserve most teacher performance while substantially reducing model size and inference cost, but effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data used for distillation, and matching between teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-label matching, intermediate representation transfer, feature-level distillation, and multi-teacher ensemble strategies. While knowledge distillation frequently yields substantial gains in model size, latency, and memory with modest performance loss, its effectiveness depends on critical factors including teacher quality, student capacity, data characteristics, and the specific form of knowledge transferred. Current research advances include theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works, task-aware student design, robustness considerations, and adaptation to privacy-sensitive and distributed training scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Methods and Practices for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible set of techniques to transfer knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student. Work across modalities and tasks has shown KD can yield compact models that approach teacher performance, enable deployment on resource-limited devices, help mitigate data-availability or privacy constraints, and act as a vehicle for transferring ensemble or multi-teacher knowledge into a single model. Practical KD methods vary in what they transfer (logits, intermediate features, or rankings), whether they require original training data, and how they structure training (offline, online, adversarial, or curriculum-based). Empirical and methodological work highlights (1) the effectiveness of feature-level supervision in many settings, (2) the value of synthetic or replayed data when real data are unavailable, (3) that ensemble and online schemes can speed training and improve robustness, and (4) that augmentation, sample selection, and task-specific losses materially affect distilled-student outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Efficient Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in computational cost, memory requirements, and inference latency while maintaining competitive performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation has evolved from a simple heuristic technique into a versatile, mature framework with diverse methodologies and broad applicability across computer vision, natural language processing, and multimodal learning domains. Success with knowledge distillation depends on careful matching of compression strategies to task-specific constraints and deployment requirements rather than reliance on a single universal approach.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Necessary but Context-Dependent Tool for Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a central technique for compressing large neural networks into efficient student models deployable on resource-constrained devices. While knowledge distillation successfully transfers knowledge from teacher to student across diverse domains including NLP and computer vision, its effectiveness is neither universal nor automatic. Careful attention to data characteristics, teacher-student capacity relationships, and task-specific design choices is essential for reliable compression performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is a necessary component of any practical compression toolbox, but must be combined with thoughtful method selection, multiple transfer mechanisms, and domain-aware adaptation to achieve production-ready results.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression are essential techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. These methods transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, enabling substantial reductions in model size, computational cost, and inference time while maintaining competitive performance. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and question answering. The techniques address fundamental practical challenges in making state-of-the-art models viable for real-world deployment with limited latency, memory, and energy budgets.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a fundamental training paradigm in which a large, well-trained teacher model transfers learned knowledge to a smaller, more efficient student model. This technique has emerged as essential for model compression, enabling the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments without sacrificing accuracy. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, and speech recognition, serving as a versatile solution for reducing computational costs and storage requirements while maintaining competitive performance levels.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other internal signals. Across vision and language, practitioners use a toolbox of techniques—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, layer-wise mapping or progressive replacement, multi/online-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis—to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible when distillation is combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture design), but open problems remain in robustness transfer, domain shift, low-frequency and structural knowledge, and principled teacher-student selection for varied deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Framework for Efficient Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, knowledge distillation enables deployment in resource-constrained environments without significant accuracy loss. The approach has proven effective across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning, offering substantial performance improvements and computational efficiency gains. This paper argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a core and indispensable strategy for practical model compression, particularly when combined with complementary techniques and carefully tailored to specific task requirements and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Empirical Findings, and Practical Tradeoffs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques have become central to making large deep models—especially pretrained language models—practical for resource-constrained deployment and domain-specific use. Work in this area spans teacher-student soft-label distillation, architectural compression and replacement, layer-mapping strategies, data-free and robustness-aware procedures, and combinations with low-precision arithmetic. Empirical results demonstrate substantial reductions in size and latency while often preserving most task performance, but practical challenges remain around teacher–student mismatch, domain shift, access to original training data, adversarial robustness, and choosing task-specific compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression represent critical techniques for deploying large neural networks in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these approaches enable significant reductions in model size and computational cost while maintaining competitive accuracy across diverse applications including computer vision, natural language processing, and machine translation. The field has evolved from basic teacher-student knowledge transfer to sophisticated multi-faceted approaches incorporating feature-level matching, data-free methods, sample selection strategies, and robustness-aware training protocols.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) reduces model size and inference cost by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a compact student. A broad family of KD methods has been developed, ranging from matching teacher output distributions to aligning intermediate representations and designing layer-wise or relational objectives. Practitioners combine KD with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthetic or unlabeled data) to produce deployable models that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Empirical work shows KD improves generalization under limited-data regimes, recovers accuracy for low-precision networks, and can be adapted to heterogeneous or structured tasks such as graph link prediction. Key challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, dependence on data availability or privacy, and preserving rare or domain-specific behaviors; current directions emphasize student-aware teacher design, feature-level transfer, data augmentation, and task-aware objectives to mitigate these issues.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a fundamental model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. This approach enables deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. KD encompasses multiple complementary techniques including soft-label matching, feature-level supervision, intermediate representation alignment, and data-centric strategies. The method addresses critical real-world challenges such as computational efficiency, memory constraints, inference latency, privacy preservation, and device heterogeneity, with applications spanning computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and specialized domains. Success depends on careful selection of transfer targets, appropriate teacher-student pairing, data availability, and matching distillation strategies to specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Theory, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural networks into smaller models that preserve predictive performance and desirable properties of the teacher. KD encompasses soft-label supervision, intermediate-feature matching, layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher fusion, online co-training, and teacher-free/self-distillation, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, generation, recommendation) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, low-precision arithmetic, privacy, and domain shift. Successful distillation requires task-aware choices of what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to generate or select data for transfer, and how to combine objectives to trade off fidelity and generalization. Remaining challenges include principled selection of distilled signals, data-free and privacy-preserving workflows, robustness under domain shift, and automated, task-adaptive compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Composable Core for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile foundation for compressing large neural models into efficient students suitable for real-world deployment. As models grow in size and application contexts diversify, distillation provides a set of interoperable mechanisms — from soft-target transfer to intermediate feature matching, self-distillation, and teacher-ensemble consolidation — that can be combined with architecture search, quantization, and task-aware filtering to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance, careful choices about what to transfer, which data to use, and how to adapt the student architecture are necessary to avoid failure modes such as degraded handling of low-frequency phenomena or overfitting teacher artifacts. A composable, task- and data-aware distillation strategy that integrates representation-level objectives, selective data curation, and architecture adaptation yields the best practical trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Soto
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students, knowledge distillation enables deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing and computer vision. This approach addresses fundamental practical challenges such as inference latency, memory consumption, and computational requirements without significant accuracy loss. When combined with complementary compression strategies and applied thoughtfully to specific task requirements, knowledge distillation becomes an indispensable tool for bringing state-of-the-art models into real-world systems operating under resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Practical, Responsible Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core technique for reducing the size and inference cost of high‑capacity models while retaining much of their predictive power. KD extends beyond simple teacher→student soft‑label matching to include representation‑level transfer, contrastive alignment, data‑free synthesis, and privacy‑aware schemes that make compression feasible when original training data are unavailable or sensitive. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and guided by task‑aware choices about what and when to transfer, KD enables deployable models for resource‑constrained and safety‑sensitive settings. However, realizing these benefits requires attention to teacher–student capacity gaps, the form of transferred knowledge, and domain or token‑frequency effects; principled design and evaluation are therefore essential for reliable compression in practice.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Default for Model Compression: Evidence and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a compact, flexible pathway to convert large teacher models into deployable student models that retain much of the teacher’s capabilities while meeting practical constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Empirical results across vision, language, and multimodal tasks show that KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs when combined with careful teacher–student alignment, complementary compression techniques, and task-aware data strategies. However, KD is not automatic: effectiveness depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data availability and domain shift, and mitigating transferred errors or undesirable behaviors. When used as the default compression tool, KD should be coupled with principled evaluation and complementary methods to produce reliable production-ready models.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Dixon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for turning large, high-performing models into compact, deployable students. When combined with complementary strategies (data augmentation, task-aware pre-training, multi-teacher signals, architecture search, and divergence choices), KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference latency while preserving much of teacher performance. Best practice is not a single recipe but an integrated, constraint-aware pipeline that selects distilled signals, data strategies, and student architectures to meet deployment objectives.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Keystone for Compressing Deep and NLP Models, with Limits and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile framework for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD supports a broad family of techniques — from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature mimicry, ensemble teaching, data-free and privacy-preserving variants, and integration with architecture search or pruning — that together enable deployment under latency, memory, and data-privacy constraints. However, realizing KD’s empirical benefits in real systems requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student representations, and how to handle limited or private data; poor choices can degrade performance or introduce bias. This position argues that KD is essential for practical compression in deep learning and NLP, but must be applied with task-aware, data-aware, and optimization-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a versatile, empirically proven approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher networks. Across computer vision, natural language processing, graph learning, and multimodal tasks, KD techniques transfer different forms of teacher knowledge — from soft output distributions to intermediate representations — and combine with data-centric strategies (e.g., selective sampling, data synthesis, and curriculum design) to meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. Practical use of KD requires careful matching of teacher signals to student capacity, handling of limited or private data, and often integration with other compression or architecture-aware methods to realize robust, efficient models in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, addressing critical deployment challenges including model size, inference latency, and computational resource requirements. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies and mechanisms, from soft-label matching to intermediate representation alignment, and has demonstrated broad applicability across natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains. When applied thoughtfully with careful attention to architectural choices, data availability, and task-specific constraints, knowledge distillation enables practical deployment of state-of-the-art models while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while transferring learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practice
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable versions without significant loss of task performance. This approach transfers knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks, enabling efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and multimodal learning. Knowledge distillation addresses critical real-world constraints including latency, memory, privacy, and device heterogeneity, making it indispensable for practical neural network deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and practical technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from teacher models to students across diverse domains, knowledge distillation addresses critical challenges in deploying sophisticated deep learning systems to resource-constrained environments. This paper argues that knowledge distillation functions best as a flexible, composable framework encompassing multiple mechanisms and methodologies, with effectiveness dependent on careful alignment between distillation targets, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile, Practical Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a foundational technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models that maintain competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a lightweight student model, KD addresses critical practical constraints in modern deep learning deployment, including computational efficiency, memory constraints, and latency requirements. This approach has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, while remaining adaptable to various compression objectives and data availability scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory use, and latency while preserving task performance. A range of mechanisms — matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, synthesizing surrogate data, and privacy-aware or multi-teacher schemes — enable practitioners to adapt distillation to domain- and task-specific constraints. Successful application depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle data availability or privacy, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. Remaining challenges include bridging large capacity gaps, preserving rare or safety-critical behavior, data-free distillation, and robust cross-domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A diverse array of distillation mechanisms—matching soft logits, feature- and attention-level mimicry, layer- and module-level mappings, multi-teacher fusion, and synthetic-data or data-free strategies—has been developed to address deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous device capacities. Practical pipelines combine these mechanisms with task- and architecture-aware choices to retain teacher capabilities while meeting real-world constraints. This synthesis summarizes central methods, empirical findings, system-level approaches, and recurring practical recommendations drawn from recent work.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Methods, Evidence, and Open Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and adapts large teacher models into smaller, more deployable students by transferring predictive distributions, intermediate representations, or structural behavior. Across vision, language, speech, and graph domains, distillation variants enable latency- and memory-constrained deployment, improve transfer and robustness, and can be combined with architecture search or progressive module replacement to balance fidelity and efficiency. Practical success depends on choices about distillation targets, data availability (including data-free approaches), teacher–student capacity alignment, and task-aware training; these considerations frame ongoing research toward automated, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive compression strategies.
