papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved from a single compression trick into a broad, practical toolkit that enables deployment of high-performing models under real-world constraints. KD techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller students, and they can be adapted to address deployment constraints such as device heterogeneity, privacy, domain shift, fairness, and limited or missing training data. When combined with task-aware design choices and complementary compression methods, KD routinely produces compact models suitable for latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained applications across vision, speech, and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications that require fast inference and limited computational resources.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and broadly applicable technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while preserving predictive performance. By transferring knowledge from large teacher models to compact student networks, knowledge distillation enables efficient deployment across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommendation systems. This approach addresses critical practical constraints of modern machine learning by reducing storage requirements, computational costs, and inference latency, making sophisticated deep learning systems accessible for resource-constrained environments and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Deploying Deep Learning and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become critical techniques for enabling the deployment of large, computationally expensive deep learning and NLP models in resource-constrained environments. These methods enable smaller student models to effectively transfer knowledge from larger teacher models, addressing fundamental challenges of inference speed, memory consumption, and computational requirements while maintaining competitive performance. This essay argues that knowledge distillation should be considered a central and versatile tool in modern machine learning, particularly for practical deployment scenarios across diverse applications.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models. KD has matured into a flexible family of techniques—logit or soft-target matching, intermediate feature and attention transfer, multi-teacher strategies, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants—that can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance across vision, language, speech, and other modalities, but practical success depends on student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and careful engineering of objectives and schedules.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Approaches
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, more efficient students while retaining much of the teachers' performance. Recent work expands the KD toolkit beyond matching soft logits to include feature- and layer-level mimicry, task-aware selection of teacher knowledge, data-free and multi-teacher strategies, and augmentation-driven improvements. Practical advances target domain-specific challenges in language models and cross-modal systems, emphasize efficient training and deployment on heterogeneous hardware, and reinterpret KD as a form of regularization that can sometimes be partially replaced or simulated. This review synthesizes these directions and highlights recurring design principles for effective distillation in both NLP and general deep learning settings.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Critical Technique for Deep Learning Model Compression and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large deep learning models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student models, enabling efficient deployment across diverse applications. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents an essential strategy for addressing the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment requirements in both computer vision and natural language processing domains.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while transferring learned knowledge. This approach enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across domains including computer vision and natural language processing. Knowledge distillation operates through teacher-student learning frameworks that transfer knowledge beyond simple class labels to encompass soft targets, intermediate representations, and structural behaviors. The technique addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency while maintaining competitive performance.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Nuanced Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. As a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer logits, intermediate representations, relational structure, or teacher-curated data to produce efficient models suitable for constrained hardware and latency-sensitive applications. Its practical success depends on matching distillation objectives to student capacity, addressing data or privacy constraints, and complementing KD with task-aware architecture choices, robustness-aware training, or pruning and quantization. KD can markedly reduce model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but it requires careful design to avoid propagating teacher errors or losing rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Essential Framework for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models while maintaining competitive performance. By enabling efficient knowledge transfer from high-capacity teacher models to compact student networks, this approach directly addresses critical real-world deployment challenges including computational cost, memory constraints, inference latency, and privacy concerns. The technique has proven essential across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications, making it indispensable for modern machine learning deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Transferring Knowledge for Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a larger teacher model to a smaller student model, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression through distillation has proven effective across diverse applications including natural language processing, computer vision, and multimodal learning. This paper surveys the principles, methods, and applications of knowledge distillation and related compression techniques in deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: Enhancing Student Model Performance Through Teacher-Guided Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining or even improving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from a well-trained teacher model to a lightweight student model through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate layer alignment, and task-aware filtering. Applications span across natural language processing, computer vision, and domain-specific tasks, addressing critical deployment challenges related to latency, computational resources, and model size constraints in real-world production environments.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other internal signals. Across vision and language, practitioners use a toolbox of techniques—soft-target/logit matching, feature- and attention-level alignment, layer-wise mapping or progressive replacement, multi/online-teacher schedules, and data-free synthesis—to reduce parameter counts and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. Empirical work shows substantial efficiency gains are possible when distillation is combined with complementary methods (pre-training, pruning, quantization, architecture design), but open problems remain in robustness transfer, domain shift, low-frequency and structural knowledge, and principled teacher-student selection for varied deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller student models by transferring task-relevant information through soft targets, intermediate feature signals, or other auxiliary objectives. KD enables deployment of performant models under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, and it forms a flexible engineering toolkit that can be combined with pretraining, multi-teacher fusion, domain adaptation, and robustness-oriented training. Practical success depends on choosing what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize distillation data, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to evaluate students under the target deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. KD uses a range of transfer targets and training schemes to trade off accuracy, latency, and model size, and it is routinely combined with complementary compression methods to meet deployment constraints. While KD consistently enables substantial efficiency gains across vision, language, and graph domains, its practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how teachers and students are aligned, and how to handle limited or sensitive data.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reassessing Knowledge Distillation: Regularization, Teacher Quality, and Task-Driven Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile tool for compressing models and transferring capabilities from large teachers to smaller students across vision, graph, 3D, and NLP tasks. Its effectiveness arises not only from transmitting teacher class similarities but also from the regularizing properties of soft targets and from mimicking intermediate representations. Recent advances demonstrate that KD can be applied without direct access to a strong pretrained teacher or original training data, and that task-specific distillation objectives (contrastive, adversarial, feature-level) often outperform naive logit matching. At the same time, optimization barriers, teacher errors, and domain shifts can limit or bias distilled students, so practitioners should choose distillation formulations and teacher-student pairings that align with the target task and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical Necessity for Deep Learning and NLP Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving performance. This approach transfers knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to compact students, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and reducing inference latency, memory footprint, and computational overhead. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies including soft-target matching, feature-level mimicry, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher strategies, and data-free approaches, with broad applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized domains. The technique addresses critical deployment challenges while maintaining competitive accuracy across various downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a single teacher-student recipe into a flexible family of techniques that enable deployment of high-performing, resource-efficient models across domains including NLP, vision, and federated settings. KD can compress large pretrained models into lightweight architectures, transfer task-specific behavior, enable data-free or zero-shot transfers when original data are unavailable, and improve interpretability or domain generalization when adapted appropriately. However, distillation is not universally sufficient: optimization barriers, dataset artifacts, and bias transfer can limit gains unless addressed by careful method design. I argue that KD is a necessary part of any practical compression toolbox for modern deep learning, but must be combined with task-adaptive search, careful teacher selection, privacy-aware synthesis, and bias mitigation to realize reliable, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Advances, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compacts large neural networks into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD variants—ranging from soft-target matching to intermediate-feature alignment and layer-wise mapping—enable substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Recent algorithmic innovations address data scarcity, domain adaptation, and cross-modal transfer; complementary pipelines combine KD with pretraining, architecture design, and data augmentation to close the gap to teacher models. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts, and matching representational capacity between teachers and students; practical success depends on careful alignment of objectives, data, and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central and practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. The approach enables deployment in resource-constrained environments across computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized domains by transferring knowledge from well-trained teacher models to compact student architectures. Knowledge distillation encompasses diverse methodologies ranging from output-level soft-target matching to intermediate representation alignment, layer-wise supervision, and data-free synthesis approaches. When strategically combined with complementary techniques and careful architectural design, knowledge distillation provides robust solutions to real-world deployment challenges including latency reduction, memory constraints, and privacy preservation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Powerful Approach for Model Compression and Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for training compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from larger teacher networks to smaller student networks. This approach enables the deployment of high-performance models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining competitive accuracy. The technique has proven effective across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, and specialized applications such as medical diagnosis and robotic control. By distilling dark knowledge from teacher models, student networks can achieve performance that rivals their teachers while requiring significantly fewer computational resources and parameters.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Multi-Domain Imperative
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing deep models and enabling their deployment in resource-constrained settings. By transferring predictive and representational knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students, KD reduces inference costs while often preserving — and sometimes improving — accuracy and robustness. Across computer vision, speech, NLP, and large-scale distributed training, KD enables designers to balance performance and efficiency, but realizing its full potential requires careful choices about what is distilled (logits, features, relations), which data or surrogates are used, and how multi-teacher or online protocols are organized.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Essential Techniques for Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have emerged as essential techniques for deploying large, powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. By transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models, these methods address the fundamental challenge of making state-of-the-art models practical for real-world applications while maintaining competitive performance. This position argues that knowledge distillation is not merely a complementary technique but a central and versatile strategy that, when carefully designed with complementary compression methods, enables effective deployment across diverse domains in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Walsh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core Strategy for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models to lightweight student networks, KD enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning and NLP systems on resource-constrained devices without substantial accuracy loss. This approach addresses critical challenges in balancing model capacity with computational efficiency across diverse domains while supporting practical constraints such as privacy preservation and data scarcity. While KD is not a universal solution, when combined with complementary compression strategies and careful design choices, it represents the most practical and broadly applicable approach to achieving efficient neural networks suitable for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Approach to Efficient Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing deep neural networks and making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This approach transfers knowledge from larger, complex teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models, enabling significant reductions in model size and computational overhead while maintaining competitive performance. Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and domain adaptation, where the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment becomes increasingly important.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning and NLP: Powerful, Context-Dependent, and Best Deployed as an Integrated Strategy
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practically essential approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD methods range from soft-target matching to representation alignment and staged or multi-teacher procedures. Their empirical success across vision and language tasks makes KD a central tool for production deployment on resource-constrained hardware, but its effectiveness depends on careful matching of objectives, data, and student capacity. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolkit to be combined with privacy, robustness, and fairness-aware practices rather than a one-size-fits-all solution.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher performance. KD encompasses multiple families of techniques — soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, module replacement, online/peer distillation, and ensemble-to-single-model transfer — and has been applied successfully across NLP tasks (including large transformer compression and machine translation), graph and recommender systems, and large-scale distributed training. Realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires matching the distillation objective to student capacity and deployment constraints, choosing appropriate data or surrogate data strategies, and addressing interactions with training regularizers and teacher quality.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Enabling Efficient Deep Learning Through Strategic Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient student models while preserving competitive performance. This technique enables the transfer of knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to resource-constrained students through various mechanisms including soft target matching, intermediate feature alignment, and self-distillation approaches. By addressing the critical challenge of deploying computationally intensive models on memory and latency-limited devices, knowledge distillation has become indispensable across diverse domains in deep learning and natural language processing, offering practical solutions for real-world applications where efficiency is paramount.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher networks to smaller, efficient student networks, enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive performance. This approach has become a foundational strategy in deep learning and natural language processing, addressing critical challenges such as reducing computational costs, memory footprint, and inference latency. Knowledge distillation supports diverse applications across computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, and specialized domains, and can be combined with complementary compression techniques to achieve practical, production-ready compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Multi-Domain Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer across diverse domains in deep learning. By enabling smaller student networks to learn from larger, more complex teacher models, this approach addresses the critical challenge of deploying computationally expensive models on resource-constrained devices. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is an essential strategy for practical deep learning deployment, demonstrating its effectiveness across computer vision, natural language processing, medical imaging, and multi-modal applications. The technique not only reduces model size and inference time significantly but also often maintains or even improves performance compared to baseline approaches.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable models. When combined with careful design of student capacity, layer alignment, and complementary compression methods, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, distillation is not a universal remedy: its effectiveness depends on choices about what is transferred, available data, and how student and teacher internals align. Practical deployments benefit from treating KD as a multi-strategy engineering problem—selecting appropriate distillation targets, leveraging multi-teacher or data-free options when necessary, and addressing optimization gaps and low-frequency phenomena through task-aware interventions.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default, Task-Aware Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the primary tool for compressing large models into efficient students for deployment in deep learning and NLP. KD offers flexible mechanisms to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from teachers to students, enabling substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. However, KD is not a one-size-fits-all recipe: its success depends on careful, task-aware design choices (e.g., which signals to transfer, teacher selection, data regimes, and complementary compression techniques) and on explicit strategies to detect and mitigate teacher error propagation. When applied thoughtfully and combined with other compression and deployment-aware methods, KD yields practical, high-fidelity compressed models across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, Applications, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring information beyond hard labels. A mature toolkit now includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data strategies, and privacy-aware variants. Distillation has been applied to vision, language, graphs, generative models, and healthcare, producing substantial inference and deployment gains while exposing limits arising from optimization, teacher–student mismatch, and data constraints. Progress requires carefully matching the distilled signals to student capacity, combining distillation with complementary compression methods, and addressing theoretical and practical failure modes to ensure robustness, fairness, and privacy.

Knowledge distillation is particularly valuable across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and domain adaptation, where the trade-off between model complexity and practical deployment becomes increasingly important.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression represent a broad set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, more complex neural networks to smaller, more efficient models. These approaches enable deployment of high-performing deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments while maintaining competitive accuracy. Applications span diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, machine translation, speech recognition, and graph neural networks. Knowledge distillation has evolved from a heuristic compression technique to a versatile, modality-agnostic toolkit that addresses critical challenges in model efficiency, latency reduction, privacy preservation, and task-specific performance optimization.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Dependent Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, deployable student models while preserving much of their performance. KD encompasses diverse mechanisms including soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher fusion, and self-distillation, each adapted to specific task requirements and deployment constraints. While KD is widely applicable across vision, language, and multimodal domains, its effectiveness depends critically on careful alignment of teacher-student capacity, thoughtful selection of distilled signals, appropriate data handling strategies, and consideration of domain shift and fairness concerns. This position argues that KD, when properly designed and combined with complementary compression methods, represents a practical and versatile toolkit for enabling deployment of sophisticated models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, though its success is neither automatic nor universal.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into efficient students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. KD techniques—spanning logits-based soft-target transfer, intermediate feature alignment, and data-free synthesis—enable deployment of high-performing models on resource-constrained devices while also offering benefits in robustness and interpretability. When paired with task-aware design and careful teacher selection, distillation can produce compact models that meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints without large sacrifices in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Manning
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from computationally expensive teacher models. This approach addresses critical deployment challenges in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains including natural language processing, computer vision, and specialized applications. While knowledge distillation offers substantial practical benefits in reducing model size, latency, and computational cost while maintaining competitive performance, its effectiveness depends on careful design choices and recognition of important limitations that require pragmatic, task-adaptive application strategies.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression strategies transform large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision, NLP, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD methods—including soft-target matching, feature- and layer-level alignment, online and teacher-free variants, multi-teacher schemes, and privacy- or communication-constrained protocols—enable practical deployment under latency, memory, and data constraints. Successful distillation requires matching the distillation signals to student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate data, and combining KD with other compression mechanisms when needed. This synthesis summarizes core mechanisms, common variants, representative applications, practical recommendations, and known limitations.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Attention-Guided Answer Distillation for Machine Reading Comprehension
papers_seen.abstract: Despite that current reading comprehension systems have achieved significant advancements, their promising performances are often obtained at the cost of making an ensemble of numerous models. Besides, existing approaches are also vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper tackles these problems by leveraging knowledge distillation, which aims to transfer knowledge from an ensemble model to a single model. We first demonstrate that vanilla knowledge distillation applied to answer span prediction is effective for reading comprehension systems. We then propose two novel approaches that not only penalize the prediction on confusing answers but also guide the training with alignment information distilled from the ensemble. Experiments show that our best student model has only a slight drop of 0.4% F1 on the SQuAD test set compared to the ensemble teacher, while running 12x faster during inference. It even outperforms the teacher on adversarial SQuAD datasets and NarrativeQA benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-Aware Imperative for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques are indispensable for deploying modern deep learning models in resource-constrained settings. By transferring soft-targets, intermediate representations, or other distilled signals from larger teacher models to compact students, KD preserves much of the teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and latency. Effective distillation is not a single algorithm but a family of methods that must be chosen and tuned with respect to task requirements, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; when combined with complementary compression strategies, KD enables real-world use of powerful models across vision, language, and multimodal domains.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Practical Strategies and Empirical Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a core, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, recommender systems, and other domains, practitioners combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and with data-centric strategies (augmentation, synthesis, task-aware selection) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation depends on coordinated choices about what to transfer (logits, features, layers, or modules), how teachers and students are matched, and how to handle limited or private data; addressing these choices with multi-strategy pipelines produces more robust, efficient models for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile approach for both model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This paper argues that knowledge distillation represents a superior alternative to traditional compression methods because it enables effective compression while maintaining model performance, facilitates transfer of complex learned representations across architectures, and proves applicable across diverse domains including computer vision, natural language processing, graph neural networks, and reinforcement learning. Unlike methods that simply reduce model parameters without guidance, knowledge distillation leverages teacher-student frameworks to encode valuable "dark knowledge" that improves generalization and produces more robust, efficient models.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential Paradigm for Model Compression and Practical Deep Learning Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and versatile technique for compressing large neural networks into smaller, more efficient models while maintaining competitive performance. By transferring knowledge from high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models, knowledge distillation addresses the critical challenge of deploying state-of-the-art deep learning systems in resource-constrained environments across diverse domains. This approach extends beyond basic model compression to enable practical deployment scenarios, privacy-preserving learning, and knowledge transfer across heterogeneous architectures. The technique has proven effective across natural language processing, computer vision, graph neural networks, and multimodal learning, establishing it as an indispensable tool for modern deep learning systems.
